mztlVxoA85.one_liner: Training-free structured pruning of vision foundation models that jointly searches layerwise capacity and closed-form low-rank weight recovery.
mztlVxoA85.problem: Existing structured pruning fails at aggressive compression because it treats subnetwork selection and recovery of removed behavior as separate axes.
mztlVxoA85.method: Given a VFM, a calibration set, and a parameter budget, it searches task-specific capacity allocations across layers using an adaptive recovery-aware fitness criterion, then reconstructs removed behavior with iterative closed-form low-rank corrections merged into the surviving weights.
mztlVxoA85.key_idea: Score pruning candidates by how well the removed contribution can be recovered, then merge closed-form low-rank corrections into the surviving weights.
mztlVxoA85.evidence: Evaluated across twelve benchmarks and four models from DINOv3 and MetaCLIP-2, where it ranks first among all evaluated structured-pruning methods (abstract is truncated after this point).
mztlVxoA85.claimed_gains: Ranks first among evaluated structured-pruning methods and produces a dense task model in minutes on a single GPU without training; no numeric gains are visible in the truncated abstract.

ErDssTAXQA.one_liner: Learns reusable forensic coordinates from history to cut labels needed when image generators and processing conditions change.
ErDssTAXQA.problem: Past decision rules of AI-generated image detectors become unreliable as generators and processing conditions change, and it is unclear what representations should retain to reduce future label needs.
ErDssTAXQA.method: Continual Updating of Evidence (CUE) keeps the visual encoder and initial detector fixed, estimates within-class variation from historical and current statistics, and uses current labels for the remaining update (abstract truncated). The framework supports few-shot adaptation, continual learning, and unlearning.
ErDssTAXQA.key_idea: Coordinates learned from finite history, using within-class variation estimated from historical and current statistics, retain information that past decision rules omit and reduce adaptation labels.
ErDssTAXQA.evidence: Theory in a Gaussian model: finite-history coordinates reduce adaptation labels versus retaining optimal past decision rules alone, with bounds separating coordinate learning from current-label fitting and a shared-space sufficiency result for full-space optimal AUROC; empirical details are cut off in the abstract.

UVPZsieErl.one_liner: Learner-side batch selection for asynchronous multi-turn on-policy distillation that spreads a turn budget across rollouts and favors high teacher-student disagreement.
UVPZsieErl.problem: In asynchronous multi-turn on-policy distillation, arrival-order batching lets a few early or long rollouts dominate updates while other valid rollouts go stale, wasting generated experience.
UVPZsieErl.method: DivOPD spreads a fixed turn budget across more rollouts and, within each rollout, prioritizes turns with larger cumulative teacher-student disagreement, excluding turns without usable teacher feedback. The per-turn loss and optimizer stay fixed, and an optional extension briefly hands control to the teacher for no-progress rollouts.
UVPZsieErl.key_idea: Select which student-visited turns get training weight by diversity across rollouts and cumulative teacher-student disagreement within rollouts, leaving the loss and optimizer unchanged.
UVPZsieErl.evidence: Six teacher-student settings on simulated ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and WebShop with 1.5B-7B students.
UVPZsieErl.claimed_gains: Raises cross-setting mean peak success rate from 77.4 to 84.4 and mean success over the last five evaluations from 71.5 to 78.6, with geometric-mean speedups of 1.84x in training tokens and 1.87x in learner GPU time relative to vanilla OPD.

2u0MFYC5BB.one_liner: Proves last-iterate convergence of predictive discounted regret matching+ in perturbed regularized extensive-form games for any step size and initialization.
2u0MFYC5BB.problem: CFR with regret matching+ only has average-strategy convergence, and the predictive and discounted variants PCFR+, DCFR+, and PDCFR+ lacked the last-iterate guarantee that RTCFR+ proved for plain CFR+ in the reward-transformation framework.
2u0MFYC5BB.method: They study one family of local minimizers, predictive discounted regret matching+, that contains all these variants, show its strategy sequence depends on step size and initialization only through their ratio, and use this invariance to prove last-iterate convergence to the unique equilibrium in every perturbed regularized EFG under simultaneous updates when the total discount sum_t(1-d_t) is finite.
2u0MFYC5BB.key_idea: Strategies of predictive discounted regret matching+ depend on step size and initialization only through their ratio, which makes last-iterate convergence hold for any step size and initialization.
2u0MFYC5BB.evidence: Theoretical proofs of convergence; the DCFR schedule satisfies the finite-discount condition exactly when its exponent exceeds one, and without prediction a constant discount cannot converge on some perturbed regularized matrix games.

Lahcfy4bQp.one_liner: Training-free method organizing LLM molecular reasoning as structure-guided graphs of thought over SMILES inputs
Lahcfy4bQp.problem: Making molecular structure accessible to LLMs does not determine how intermediate decisions are coordinated, since observations from connected regions and separately proposed edits can interact.
Lahcfy4bQp.method: MolGoT keeps SMILES input, constructs a shared structural context, and maintains local evidence and executable molecular candidates as graph-of-thought nodes, with task-specific evaluation, integration and revision for molecular understanding, analysis, editing and generation.
Lahcfy4bQp.key_idea: Use molecular structure to ground Graph-of-Thoughts nodes and dependencies in the atoms and regions each state concerns, so findings and edits can be combined and revised.
Lahcfy4bQp.evidence: Evaluation across eleven molecular tasks spanning understanding, analysis, editing and generation; baselines and datasets are not stated in the visible abstract.

K9GXRUMM70.one_liner: OneStreamer: streaming video LLM that writes time-grounded caption memory and responds proactively, trained on a 1M-record dataset.
K9GXRUMM70.problem: Streaming video LLMs must retain evidence before its future relevance is known and respond once enough evidence appears, without compromising real-time perception.
K9GXRUMM70.method: Proactive Hierarchical Caption Memory (PHCM) produces time-grounded local-detail captions and summaries of completed events, supervised by streaming caption targets, and at inference these records complement a recent visual window. Proactive State Transition Learning (PSTL) keeps supervision at all output anchors and selects representative state-change and state-persistence tokens, and a data synthesis pipeline yields OneStreamer-1M.
K9GXRUMM70.key_idea: One shared proactive generation process jointly learns query-independent caption memory and task response, so model-written records replace revisiting historical visual features.
K9GXRUMM70.evidence: A 4B model trained on OneStreamer-1M (synthesized streaming captions and QA plus cleaned open-source data) and compared with other methods on eight evaluations; the abstract is cut off after this.
K9GXRUMM70.claimed_gains: The 4B model achieves the best results among compared methods on seven of the eight evaluations (the abstract is cut off after this).

eaiwREISSU.one_liner: HOPE treats neurons as rank-1 Hilbert-Schmidt operators to unify pruning and merging as low-rank projection for data-free compression.
eaiwREISSU.problem: Standard network compression heuristics suffer from scale symmetries and architectural biases, which hinders deconstructing the knowledge stored in trained weights.
eaiwREISSU.method: Moves compression into a Hilbert space of continuous functions, modeling each neuron as a rank-1 Hilbert-Schmidt operator so pruning and neuron merging become low-rank subspace projection, and adds macro block eviction for multi-layer structures such as residual pathways under the same metric.
eaiwREISSU.key_idea: Neurons as rank-1 Hilbert-Schmidt operators give one projection-based metric that is comparable across layers of different types and sizes, including whole residual blocks.
eaiwREISSU.evidence: Proof-of-concept experiments in model compression and fine-tuning, with no datasets or models named in the abstract.

DAA5EWl9Ae.one_liner: PILCH uses one-write ridge-regression moments so lifelong cross-modal hashing returns identical results under any task partition.
DAA5EWl9Ae.problem: In lifelong cross-modal hashing, segmenting the same ordered stream into different tasks changes the items returned for the same query, even at similar retrieval accuracy.
DAA5EWl9Ae.method: PILCH couples prefix learning with one-write indexing: with frozen features, permanent Dice-derived semantic targets and additive moments recover the full-prefix code-and-relation objective. A unique ridge solution and a shared sample-count clock give identical query heads, historical codes and rankings across taskifications.
DAA5EWl9Ae.key_idea: Accumulate additive moments with permanent Dice-derived targets so the ridge solution depends only on the data prefix, not on how the stream is split into tasks.
DAA5EWl9Ae.evidence: A proof of identical heads, codes and rankings across taskifications, perturbation bounds, and experiments on four datasets with three paired seeds measuring top-k retrieval reproducibility rate and Jaccard overlap alongside relevance.
DAA5EWl9Ae.claimed_gains: The analytic core returns identical sets and ordered lists at k=10,20,50, and fixed-gallery query calibration achieves the highest mean average precision on all four datasets, reaching 92.68% on MIRFlickr-25K at 64 bits.

IiQsxXRPv7.one_liner: Computes exact leave-one-out data values with rank-one updates of a Pearson-divergence density-ratio utility, composable across data holders.
IiQsxXRPv7.problem: Model-agnostic data valuation methods rely on sensitivity, influence or hierarchical approximations instead of explicit finite deletion, and values computed independently across multiple data holders are incomparable.
IiQsxXRPv7.method: FastDV derives an additive-statistic formulation that decomposes target-set dependence into sample-wise statistics, so deletions are analytically decomposable and partitions composable. Sample value is a Pearson-divergence-based density-ratio utility computed by exact rank-one updates, extended to multi-party global valuation without pooling raw client data.
IiQsxXRPv7.key_idea: Define value as a density-ratio utility built from additive sample-wise statistics, so removing one sample is an exact rank-one update and partitions combine into globally comparable values.
IiQsxXRPv7.evidence: Experiments on typical valuation tasks and data marketplaces; the abstract is cut off before specifics.

uGse9a1yMm.one_liner: LoFT-GS stores visibility on a local texture grid inside each 2D Gaussian during light-space splatting for relightable Gaussian splatting.
uGse9a1yMm.problem: A single visibility value per Gaussian collapses illuminated and occluded regions into one shadow response when a cast-shadow boundary crosses the Gaussian.
uGse9a1yMm.method: LoFT-GS records visibility on a local texture grid within each 2D Gaussian and combines it with a Gaussian-level range predictor in a range-conditioned shadow formulation. Local texels carry visibility and diffuse appearance and modulate specular amplitude and sharpness, while geometry, base directional responses, and neural predictions remain shared per Gaussian.
uGse9a1yMm.key_idea: Factor relighting so spatially varying terms (visibility, diffuse, specular modulation) live in per-Gaussian local texels while geometry and neural predictions stay shared per Gaussian.
uGse9a1yMm.evidence: Experiments across diverse scenes comparing relighting fidelity with evaluated baselines; datasets are not named in the abstract.

edIoUy5lh2.one_liner: Replaces the sum over trajectories with a max (tropical semiring) in RL so solutions from different rollouts can be composed.
edIoUy5lh2.problem: Expected-return RL reports only how often a policy succeeds, not which solution worked, and reinforcing one solution can make the model forget another, which suits compositional reasoning poorly.
edIoUy5lh2.method: Tropical RL takes the maximum instead of the sum over alternative solutions, so a state's value is the log-probability of its most likely verified solution plus a replayable path. Tropic is the training algorithm for deterministic, resettable environments with verifiable outcomes.
edIoUy5lh2.key_idea: Switch the value algebra from sum to max (tropical semiring) so the best prefix and best suffix meeting at a shared state can be joined across rollouts.
edIoUy5lh2.evidence: Four agentic tasks: Sokoban, Countdown, FrozenLake, and WebShop (abstract truncated before results).

jiugBBDiIz.one_liner: TimeVista benchmarks vision-language models as judges of time series forecasts using micro- and macro-level judgments with rubrics.
jiugBBDiIz.problem: Numerical forecasting metrics often miss complex temporal patterns and align poorly with human preferences, and the LLM-as-a-Judge paradigm is largely unexplored for time series.
jiugBBDiIz.method: VLMs read plotted time series with textual context and give Micro- and Macro-Level judgments under evaluation rubrics; the authors build TimeVista (5,563 samples with rubrics) and Meta-TimeVista (1,025 forecast instances annotated by five experts).
jiugBBDiIz.key_idea: Render forecasts as plots and have a VLM judge them against rubrics at micro and macro levels using contextual information, validated against expert annotations.
jiugBBDiIz.evidence: Meta-evaluation against expert annotations versus point-wise and structure-aware numerical baselines, analyses of visual rendering and rubric design, and an assessment of recent time series foundation models under VLM judging.
jiugBBDiIz.claimed_gains: VLM judges align better with human judgments than point-wise and structure-aware numerical baselines; no numeric gain is stated.

X5cOmaVRdz.one_liner: Parameterizes distilled datasets as shared patch-level codebooks plus per-image patch index maps to cut redundant local storage.
X5cOmaVRdz.problem: Parameterized dataset distillation methods still redundantly encode recurring local structures across synthetic images, limiting storage efficiency.
X5cOmaVRdz.method: Each synthetic image is assembled from learned representative patches chosen by a patch index map, with patch representations shared across images; multiple codebooks at different stages combine their patches additively to increase representation power.
X5cOmaVRdz.key_idea: Share learnable patch-level codebooks across all synthetic images, with each image defined by an index map into the codebooks and multi-stage codebooks combined additively.
X5cOmaVRdz.evidence: Experiments on standard dataset distillation benchmarks across various distillation methods; details are not given in the abstract.
X5cOmaVRdz.claimed_gains: Claims top performance across various dataset distillation methods on standard benchmarks; no numbers are stated.

mMGYtEzsho.one_liner: macro2mind trains a language model with GRPO on prediction-market price signals to learn group-level behavioral reasoning for user simulation.
mMGYtEzsho.problem: LLM behavioral reasoning for simulating individuals is inherited from pretraining or learned from individual-level annotations that offer limited diversity and little supervision of the reasoning itself.
mMGYtEzsho.method: The model is trained with GRPO on market signals using a social behavioral decomposition: it infers representative participant groups, predicts how each interprets news and updates beliefs, reasons about their interactions and aggregates into a price. A hindsight-regret curriculum upweights transitions where hindsight-identified groups most improve the forecast.
mMGYtEzsho.key_idea: Make behavioral reasoning an explicit forecasting step (group inference, belief updates, interactions, aggregation) rewarded by market price outcomes, with a hindsight-regret curriculum weighting training transitions.
mMGYtEzsho.evidence: SWM-Bench on Polymarket, plus zero-shot transfer to four user-simulation benchmarks (Humanual, OvertonBench, PRISM and CAD).
mMGYtEzsho.claimed_gains: Reports leading directional accuracy and correlation on Polymarket and leading performance in zero-shot user-simulation transfer; no numbers are stated and the abstract is truncated.

Na7wmY7P95.one_liner: WeLike2Party animates multiple people via direct in-context video conditioning, with reference-asymmetric RoPE and identity-binding supervision.
Na7wmY7P95.problem: Multi-human image animation struggles to preserve identity-motion binding under inter-person occlusion, because existing methods rely on explicit motion representations such as 2D skeletons or parametric body meshes.
Na7wmY7P95.method: The framework conditions directly on the driving video in context without explicit pose or mesh extraction at inference, adds Reference Asymmetric RoPE Conditioning to preserve appearance details, and adds Identity Binding Supervision to tie each reference identity to its intended motion. For training, the authors build MotionTwin (14.4K cross-identity video pairs, 84.3 hours) and the MotionTwin-Bench benchmark.
Na7wmY7P95.key_idea: Feed the driving video as in-context conditioning with asymmetric RoPE for references and explicit supervision linking each identity to its motion, replacing skeleton or mesh inputs.
Na7wmY7P95.evidence: Experiments on MotionTwin-Bench and real-world videos against recent methods, trained on the synthetic MotionTwin dataset of 14.4K cross-identity video pairs (84.3 hours).
Na7wmY7P95.claimed_gains: Outperforms recent methods on MotionTwin-Bench and real-world videos; no numbers are visible in the truncated abstract.

wvQiB7TLyy.one_liner: Loop Scaling Laws jointly model recurrence, MoE sparsity, model size, and data to predict looped MoE loss.
wvQiB7TLyy.problem: Existing scaling laws model recurrence (looped transformers) or sparsity (Mixture-of-Experts) in isolation, not jointly.
wvQiB7TLyy.method: The law centers on a bounded, sparsity-conditional recurrence mapping that gives the effective-parameter gain from looping and how sparsity raises it, and it reduces to standard dense and MoE scaling laws as special cases. Fitted laws guide the design of looped MoE models under compute and memory constraints.
wvQiB7TLyy.key_idea: A bounded, sparsity-conditional recurrence mapping converts looping into effective-parameter gain, with larger gain at higher sparsity, inside a joint scaling law over size and data.
wvQiB7TLyy.evidence: Held-out loss prediction against prior laws, downstream evaluations of sparsity and recurrence, and a trillion-token-scale run comparing a looped MoE with a larger non-looped MoE.
wvQiB7TLyy.claimed_gains: Sparsity delivers about 3x active-parameter efficiency and recurrence about 2x total-parameter efficiency on reasoning, and at matched training compute at trillion-token scale a looped MoE matches a roughly 2x larger non-looped MoE.

VL1M8jZKCP.one_liner: MuPS adds explicit solution hypotheses with condition-dependent activation to physics models, recovering multiple admissible solutions from unlabeled outcomes.
VL1M8jZKCP.problem: Learning-based physics models map a condition to one solution or a sampled solution, but multi-solution problems need a condition-dependent set of admissible solutions, where a single predictor averages incompatible solutions and sampling needs many draws to reveal rare modes.
VL1M8jZKCP.method: MuPS augments existing physics-learning architectures with a small collection of explicit solution hypotheses and condition-dependent activation, learning a set-valued solution map from branch-unlabeled input-solution observations. Activation decides which hypotheses are admissible per condition, so the represented solution-set cardinality varies across the input domain.
VL1M8jZKCP.key_idea: Keep a few explicit solution hypotheses and learn a per-condition activation selecting which are admissible, so predicted solution count varies with the condition.
VL1M8jZKCP.evidence: Applied to Fourier neural operators, neural fields, and conditional diffusion models across three physical and synthetic benchmarks and three model families.
VL1M8jZKCP.claimed_gains: Substantially improves best-of-K prediction accuracy across the benchmarks and model families; no numbers are visible in the truncated abstract.

mnSqH5lBww.one_liner: LunaTP is a GPU kernel using node-centric execution, path-group parallelism, and multi-level reuse to accelerate Clebsch-Gordan tensor product convolutions.
mnSqH5lBww.problem: Clebsch-Gordan tensor product convolutions in equivariant machine-learning interatomic potentials are computationally expensive, limiting model scalability and efficiency.
mnSqH5lBww.method: LunaTP rethinks parallel execution of CGTP convolutions with node-centric execution, exploiting path-group parallelism and multi-level reuse, and also accelerates higher-order derivative computation while preserving the underlying mathematical formulation.
mnSqH5lBww.key_idea: Parallelize CGTP convolutions per node, grouping computation paths and reusing intermediate results at multiple levels, without changing the underlying mathematics.
mnSqH5lBww.evidence: Benchmarks on an NVIDIA H100 GPU against e3nn and OpenEquivariance for kernel speed and end-to-end training throughput, across models, workload scales, and GPUs.
mnSqH5lBww.claimed_gains: Kernel speedups of up to 250.0x over e3nn and 17.1x over OpenEquivariance, and end-to-end training throughput gains of up to 28.7x over e3nn and 3.11x over OpenEquivariance.

rf7VAHwOvJ.one_liner: WIRE compresses video tokens and encodes the removed visual information in temporary hypernetwork-generated LoRA updates to a frozen video LLM.
rf7VAHwOvJ.problem: Long videos give video language models long visual-embedding sequences that raise prefill, memory, and generation cost at once, since every embedding passes through every decoder layer, the KV cache, and every generated token.
rf7VAHwOvJ.method: WIRE compresses each frame's embeddings into a few carrier tokens with a question-conditioned bidirectional selective scan and contracts the decoder input. Hypernetworks at selected decoder layers read the compressed pass plus a readout of the removed full-resolution features and generate LoRA updates to attention and feedforward projections, merged after prefill so decoding runs the unmodified backbone.
rf7VAHwOvJ.key_idea: Move part of the video-conditioned computation from input activations into a temporary low-rank weight update generated by hypernetworks from the features removed by token contraction.
rf7VAHwOvJ.evidence: Experiments on Qwen3-VL-8B with 16 carrier tokens per frame; further results are cut off in the abstract.
rf7VAHwOvJ.claimed_gains: Up to 4.14x faster prefill and improved accuracy over token compression alone, per the TLDR.

kN54kfhdDB.one_liner: Near a fixed point, a looped language model's endpoint replaces its recurrent trajectory in training, KV caching, distillation, and RL.
kN54kfhdDB.problem: Looped language models pay for the whole recurrent trajectory in training, inference, and post-training even when their states converge to fixed points.
kN54kfhdDB.method: The terminal state stands in for the trajectory, enabling truncated backpropagation, terminal KV-cache reuse, distillation, and RL updates computed from saved rollout states. To shape better fixed points, the authors learn a constrained depth-sampling prior and force orthogonal updates in input injection so each recurrence receives the input intact.
kN54kfhdDB.key_idea: Use the converged terminal state in place of the trajectory, and shape fixed points with a learned depth prior and orthogonal input injection.
kN54kfhdDB.evidence: Experiments at 100M, 400M, and 1.6B parameters compared against Huginn's fixed depth prior and leading input-injection schemes.
kN54kfhdDB.claimed_gains: Terminal KV-cache reuse shrinks the cache 5x for a loop-5 core (3x for the whole cache), distillation gives up to 1.66x faster prefill, RL updates run 1.5x faster, the learned depth prior lowers perplexity by 1.1-1.9%, and orthogonal injection by up to 1.6%.

l6yQeN0R8j.one_liner: HN-CLIP adds detached text-encoder caption-similarity matrices to negative logits as adaptive margins for dense-caption retrieval.
l6yQeN0R8j.problem: InfoNCE loss saturates prematurely when fine-tuning dense-caption retrieval from a strong pretrained dual encoder, because near-duplicate captions leave the most confusable negatives unresolved.
l6yQeN0R8j.method: HN-CLIP adds a detached caption-similarity matrix from the text encoder's own text-text geometry to the negative logits, giving larger margins to more similar captions without mining, synthesizing, or resampling negatives. It needs one similarity matrix and a masked logit addition during training, with no extra data, parameters, or inference cost.
l6yQeN0R8j.key_idea: Add the text encoder's detached caption-to-caption similarity to each negative's logit, so more similar captions get larger margins and keep gradient signal.
l6yQeN0R8j.evidence: A gradient-dynamics analysis showing InfoNCE loss falls below 10^-3 on 80% of sampled batches within the first epoch, and experiments on four dense-caption retrieval benchmarks.
l6yQeN0R8j.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is truncated before the improvement over the strongest competitors is given).

mFDPi21486.one_liner: PerceptArena benchmarks web agents that must decide how much to observe, at what fidelity, and when to stop observing.
mFDPi21486.problem: Computer-use benchmarks render the environment to the agent at every step, so agents never decide what to observe and perception allocation goes unmeasured.
mFDPi21486.method: A controllable, self-hosted web environment with nine scenarios and a cross-scenario layer totaling 652 tasks, each placing decisive evidence at particular locations and information carriers. It compares the standard Harness-Supplied Observation (HSO) protocol with the proposed Agent-Controlled Perception (ACP) protocol.
mFDPi21486.key_idea: Return observation control to the agent, placing decisive evidence at specific locations and carriers so what to look at, at what fidelity, and when to stop matter.
mFDPi21486.evidence: 18 vision-language models, spanning frontier and mid-tier APIs, evaluated under both the HSO and ACP protocols on 652 tasks.
mFDPi21486.claimed_gains: Seventeen of eighteen models get higher cost-success AUC under ACP, sixteen spend fewer metered tokens, the median model spends 59% of its HSO metered tokens, average success moves only 2.1 points (0.9 excluding two degenerate baselines), and evidence recall rises from 60.0% to 64.7%.

K6mOMIOghl.one_liner: SAGE improves 2-bit vector quantization of LLM weights via energy-stratified channel grouping and per-matrix adaptive direction/radius bit splits.
K6mOMIOghl.problem: Existing vector-quantization methods still degrade on real-world tasks below 3 bits because they under-protect sensitive weight channels within jointly encoded vectors and do not adapt how a fixed bit budget is split between direction and radius.
K6mOMIOghl.method: Energy-Stratified Grouping (ESG) couples channel grouping with activation-weighted fitting, mixing channels from different energy tiers within each subvector to prioritize sensitive channels. Adaptive Bit Split (ABS) picks, per matrix, the direction-codebook and radius-precision split with the lowest activation-weighted reconstruction error under a fixed budget, and custom CUDA kernels support efficient inference.
K6mOMIOghl.key_idea: Group channels from different energy tiers into each subvector and choose per matrix the direction/radius bit split that minimizes activation-weighted reconstruction error.
K6mOMIOghl.evidence: Benchmarks covering knowledge, mathematics, code generation, instruction following, and tool use for 2-bit weight-only quantization.
K6mOMIOghl.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims top 2-bit performance without visible numbers).

ROX7Rm99uU.one_liner: Architecture-preserving VLN with MLLMs using single-turn inputs, global-local memory, action chunks, and an IL-DAgger-RL training pipeline.
ROX7Rm99uU.problem: Vision-and-language navigation methods often rely on task-specific architectures, and it is unclear whether the potential of native MLLMs for VLN has been unlocked before adding them.
ROX7Rm99uU.method: SimpleVLN combines single-turn decision inputs with fixed-budget global-local memory and action chunks that output multiple primitive actions per model call. Training mixes expert demonstrations with policy-dependent DAgger experience and a synthesis pipeline for large-scale RL tasks, through a progressive IL-DAgger-RL pipeline.
ROX7Rm99uU.key_idea: Keep the native MLLM unchanged and improve VLN through formulation (bounded global-local memory, action chunks), data (DAgger plus synthesized RL tasks), and progressive imitation-to-RL optimization.
ROX7Rm99uU.evidence: Instantiated across multiple MLLM backbones and model sizes, with experiments on formulation, data construction, and optimization; benchmark names are cut off in the available abstract.
ROX7Rm99uU.claimed_gains: The abstract reports 76.7% and a second figure that is cut off in the available text.

P2pKT1E7k5.one_liner: Uses per-frame geometry only as token-level addresses to route attention to historical frame latents for camera-controlled video generation.
P2pKT1E7k5.problem: Long-horizon camera-controlled video generation must recover previously observed content from a growing visual history, but implicit search is inefficient and persistent 3D memory accumulates geometric errors.
P2pKT1E7k5.method: GEAR keeps historical observations as frame latents and uses per-frame geometry only to establish token-level correspondences with target views. Geometric Correspondence Attention injects geometrically matched historical features into noisy target patches during denoising, and an Invisible Octree accumulates visibility evidence to reject occluded correspondences.
P2pKT1E7k5.key_idea: Use geometry only as a token-level address that decides where visual memory is read from, while attention decides what is recovered, avoiding fusion into a persistent global 3D representation.
P2pKT1E7k5.evidence: Experiments on visual quality, camera control, and revisit consistency; details are cut off in the available abstract.

usS4ezuqQp.one_liner: Radian adds real-data adversarial supervision in a frozen vision foundation model's feature space to on-policy DMD for autoregressive video distillation
usS4ezuqQp.problem: In few-step autoregressive video generation, early-block errors are reused as context and propagate into detail degradation, structural drift, and unstable motion, and DMD aligns only diffusion-latent distributions without supervising the perceptual quality of decoded videos.
usS4ezuqQp.method: Radian sparsely decodes frames from autoregressive student rollouts, extracts multi-level representations with a frozen visual foundation model, and applies lightweight discriminator heads to separate generated from real frames, alongside the on-policy DMD objective. These extra components are discarded after training, leaving the generator and inference-time denoising budget unchanged.
usS4ezuqQp.key_idea: Add an adversarial loss on decoded student frames in frozen foundation-model feature space, with light discriminator heads, to on-policy DMD so the student receives perceptual gradients.
usS4ezuqQp.evidence: Experiments on Wan2.1-1.3B covering four-step chunk-wise, one-step frame-wise, and minute-long autoregressive generation.
usS4ezuqQp.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text in the batch ends before the results)

K8auhusu7J.one_liner: Trained model that synthesizes, repairs, and self-evolves task-adaptive agent harnesses on the fly for off-the-shelf agentic LLMs.
K8auhusu7J.problem: Agent harness design (memory, planning, action protocol, tool orchestration) is manual, task-specific, and unscalable, yet can dominate the underlying model's contribution.
K8auhusu7J.method: JIT-Agent formalizes a harness as a machine-generatable artifact under a fixed four-module protocol and is trained to customize harnesses for a task, repair them for reliable execution, and self-evolve by distilling performance signals from an archive of prior harness configurations.
K8auhusu7J.key_idea: Train a model to generate harnesses as composable artifacts under a fixed four-module protocol, refining them from an expanding archive of past configurations.
K8auhusu7J.evidence: DeepSearchQA and OdysseyBench results, plus controlled evaluations against mature runtimes such as OpenCode and Claude Code across the DeepSeek V4, Mimo-V2.5, and Qwen3.6 model families.
K8auhusu7J.claimed_gains: With JIT-Agent, DeepSeek-V4-Flash surpasses GPT-5.6 on DeepSearchQA (+9.1) and OdysseyBench (+4.3), and GLM-5.2 gains up to +20.2 points.

qeTdV8fQ4T.one_liner: Flow matching on a continuity-reaction equation whose horizontal projector removes shared rigid motion from single-cell spatial transcriptomics dynamics.
qeTdV8fQ4T.problem: Connecting spatial transcriptomics snapshots acquired in different coordinate frames lets a rotation or translation of a section appear as cell movement and distort the inferred correspondence.
qeTdV8fQ4T.method: Horizontal flow matching learns changes in tissue organization, molecular state, and cell abundance up to shared rigid motion; a horizontal projector removes the rigid component from spatial prediction errors during learning and from predicted velocities during generation. The model HORIZON uses an equivariant transformer to predict velocity and growth from the current tissue, so a tissue can be generated from a single initial snapshot.
qeTdV8fQ4T.key_idea: Project shared rigid motion out of predicted velocities and spatial errors, using Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao paths that jointly estimate correspondence and relative pose as regression targets.
qeTdV8fQ4T.evidence: A simulated tissue observed in perturbed coordinate frames and four biological time courses, compared with existing methods (abstract is truncated).
qeTdV8fQ4T.claimed_gains: On four biological time courses, HORIZON attains lower reconstruction error than existing methods; no numeric values are visible because the abstract is truncated.

NT9WMkWqlG.one_liner: Derives how many in-context demonstrations match an m-example LoRA fine-tune at depth L under a rank-r linear model.
NT9WMkWqlG.problem: In-context learning and low-rank fine-tuning are rarely compared on equal statistical footing.
NT9WMkWqlG.method: Both are modeled as estimating a rank-r linear map from K demonstrations or m fine-tuning examples, and the matching demonstration count K*(m,L) is derived, including a case with register tokens where ICL equals factored gradient descent.
NT9WMkWqlG.key_idea: Place ICL and LoRA on one rank-r linear estimation model, and show attention that is linear in labels needs a fixed multiple of demonstrations per fine-tuning example.
NT9WMkWqlG.evidence: Theoretical bounds in a rank-r linear map model, including a two-sided escape-time bound; the abstract is cut off before any experiments.
NT9WMkWqlG.claimed_gains: Label-linear in-context estimators need at least d^2/[r(2d-r)] demonstrations per fine-tuning example at every depth, and at matched budget label-linear attention needs 3.4x more above a crossover depth.

mlYrAZlNlD.one_liner: Parameter-free Adaptive Interface Equalizer reweights VLM outputs by the action model's evolving sensitivity during VLA training.
mlYrAZlNlD.problem: In vision-language-action models the action model progressively concentrates its sensitivity on high-variance dimensions of the VLM outputs, and how downstream heads co-adapt to pretrained representation geometry is underexplored.
mlYrAZlNlD.method: AdaIE is a parameter-free mechanism that reweights pretrained representations according to the evolving downstream sensitivity during training, counteracting sensitivity concentration. It is motivated by controlled experiments across backbone-head combinations showing that counteracting the concentration helps under representation-task mismatch.
mlYrAZlNlD.key_idea: Reweight the pretrained VLM representation during training by the action head's current sensitivity so the head cannot concentrate on high-variance dimensions.
mlYrAZlNlD.evidence: Simulation benchmarks RoboCasa-GR1 and RoboTwin 2.0, five real-world manipulation tasks, and extensions to diffusion policies and world models.
mlYrAZlNlD.claimed_gains: Gains of up to 5.28% on RoboCasa-GR1 and 1.68% on RoboTwin 2.0, and an average gain of 19% across five real-world manipulation tasks.

fBc4oexOI4.one_liner: Models the LLM residual stream as a dynamical system, proving robust optimizers act as dampers with a negative Quasi-Lyapunov exponent.
fBc4oexOI4.problem: LLMs are fragile to tiny, semantic-preserving prompt perturbations, and the physical origin of this vulnerability and of its mitigation by robust training is unclear.
fBc4oexOI4.method: The residual stream is modeled as a discrete-time non-linear dynamical system that unifies robust strategies (SAM, Muon, noise injection, Weighted Instruction Tuning) as dampers pushing the Quasi-Lyapunov exponent negative. The authors further prove this contraction unlocks the Unconstrained Feature Model, dampening intra-class variance and forming a Simplex Equiangular Tight Frame through Progressive Neural Collapse.
fBc4oexOI4.key_idea: Robust optimizers induce dissipative residual-stream dynamics (negative Quasi-Lyapunov exponent) that causally drive Neural Collapse into attractor basins resisting prompt perturbations.
fBc4oexOI4.evidence: Mathematical proofs unifying SAM, Muon, noise injection, and WIT; the visible abstract is cut off before any empirical results.

Id9RBNSwPz.one_liner: Characterizes graph domains by a reference encoder's optimization response and predicts via task-relative labels across non-aligned label spaces.
Id9RBNSwPz.problem: Federated domain generalization on graphs assumes globally aligned label spaces, which fails for heterogeneous graph domains with different class cardinalities and semantics.
Id9RBNSwPz.method: FedDARC characterizes domains through the optimization responses of a common reference encoder, learns geometry-preserving domain states, and uses them to residually calibrate node representations. It then builds task-relative labels and aggregates query-to-context relational evidence, so inference keeps the shared model fixed and derives the domain state and labels from labeled context nodes.
Id9RBNSwPz.key_idea: Derive a domain state from a shared reference encoder's optimization response and replace fixed classifiers with query-to-context relational inference over task-relative labels.
Id9RBNSwPz.evidence: Experiments on graph datasets; details are not visible in the available abstract.

Qa9wo8eiyy.one_liner: Multi-axis out-of-distribution benchmark for protein understanding across sequence, structure and function shifts, with a retention metric (ProDPR).
Qa9wo8eiyy.problem: Protein benchmarks are IID or use a single OOD axis such as sequence identity, although test proteins diverge along sequence, structure and function.
Qa9wo8eiyy.method: POOR spans 10 protein tasks, each annotated with 24-28 OOD scenario flags, and ProDPR is a unified metric that compares generalization across single-axis OOD scenarios and their combinations. It benchmarks protein language models at several scales, structure-aware models and different fine-tuning regimes.
Qa9wo8eiyy.key_idea: Annotate each task's test examples with OOD scenario flags along sequence, structure and function axes, and score performance retention for single and combined shifts.
Qa9wo8eiyy.evidence: Benchmarks of protein language models at multiple scales, structure-aware models and fine-tuning regimes across the 10 tasks.
Qa9wo8eiyy.claimed_gains: Stronger in-distribution performance does not necessarily imply greater OOD robustness; the benchmark has 10 tasks with 24-28 OOD scenario flags each; no performance numbers stated.

5giTpBMw9l.one_liner: Performative policy learning via an evaluation-vector mediator and a differentiable surrogate for the distribution map, using batch feedback.
5giTpBMw9l.problem: Strategic classification and performative prediction rely on restrictive parametric assumptions about micro-level agent utilities or macro-level distribution maps, which limits scalability.
5giTpBMw9l.method: Identifies the evaluation vector, the policy values at all feasible points an agent can reach, as a mediator from deployed model to shifted data, and optimizes the policy by gradient steps through a differentiable classifier standing in for the high-dimensional distribution map.
5giTpBMw9l.key_idea: Use the vector of policy values over an agent's reachable points as the causal mediator, and learn a differentiable surrogate classifier for the distribution map to enable gradient-based policy optimization.
5giTpBMw9l.evidence: Theoretical convergence guarantees and experiments in challenging settings (abstract truncated before details).
5giTpBMw9l.claimed_gains: Claims superior sample efficiency from batch feedback over bandit feedback that summarizes responses into scalars; no numbers are stated.

EQZDpDpNR7.one_liner: Models stochastic gradient flow as a percolation process in which nested architectural symmetries make subnetworks merge in discrete blocks.
EQZDpDpNR7.problem: How SGD steers deep networks toward invariant sets corresponding to simpler subnetworks unfolds over time is poorly understood.
EQZDpDpNR7.method: They model stochastic gradient flow as percolation where nested symmetries force subnetworks to merge in blocks, show the transitions as variance spikes in a macroscopic order parameter, and state sufficient conditions for the trapping argument to carry over to Adam and AdamW under heavy-tailed gradient noise.
EQZDpDpNR7.key_idea: Treat SGD collapse as percolation over nested architectural symmetries, with block-wise subnetwork merging appearing as variance spikes in an order parameter.
EQZDpDpNR7.evidence: Theoretical analysis, with the stated Adam and AdamW conditions measured on a trained Transformer.

aKNMb8ruxZ.one_liner: Learned image codec with a 5.2 kMAC/pixel neural receiver and integer linear CDF predictor for single-thread CPU decoding.
aKNMb8ruxZ.problem: Learned image compression methods are computationally expensive on resource-constrained hardware, particularly CPUs.
aKNMb8ruxZ.method: PULSE pairs an ultra-low-complexity neural receiver with bit-exact CDF selection and entropy-symbol decoding through an integer linear CDF predictor and a meta prior, and recovers compression performance by iteratively improving the architecture through an agentic evolution process guided by heuristic probes with human–LLM collaboration.
aKNMb8ruxZ.key_idea: Use an integer linear CDF predictor with a meta prior for bit-exact entropy decoding, and evolve a tiny architecture through human–LLM collaboration guided by heuristic probes.
aKNMb8ruxZ.evidence: Compression performance on the CLIC Professional Validation dataset against HM, decode-time measurement on 1080p images, and an FID comparison with MS-ILLM after perceptual optimization.
aKNMb8ruxZ.claimed_gains: PULSE decodes a 1080p image in 126 ms on a single CPU thread with 5.2 kMAC/pixel, matches HM-level compression on CLIC Professional Validation, and after perceptual optimization achieves a lower FID than MS-ILLM at the same bitrate.

AisywxyyTv.one_liner: Flow matching with self-consistency across discretization scales for one- to four-step forecasting of spatiotemporal physics.
AisywxyyTv.problem: Generative emulators for physical systems face a speed–fidelity trade-off: high physical accuracy typically needs high computational cost.
AisywxyyTv.method: RecFM enforces self-consistency to align trajectories across discretization scales, reducing discretization error and enabling one- and few-step (2-4 step) generation without relying on physics-based residuals.
AisywxyyTv.key_idea: Enforce self-consistency that aligns flow trajectories across discretization scales so that few-step sampling matches multi-step solutions.
AisywxyyTv.evidence: Scientific benchmarks for spatiotemporal forecasting compared with diffusion-based emulators and vanilla flow matching (specific datasets are not named in the abstract).
AisywxyyTv.claimed_gains: Up to a 20× speedup over leading diffusion-based emulators while improving predictive accuracy, and over 15% lower mean squared error than vanilla flow matching.

w1bB3nAhvd.one_liner: Local small model solves tasks and delegates key steps to a cloud LLM, trained with step-level RL.
w1bB3nAhvd.problem: Using a frontier cloud model at every step of a long-horizon agent trajectory is costly, though not all steps need that capability.
w1bB3nAhvd.method: EdgeWise runs an SLM on the local device as primary solver and selectively delegates critical steps to a cloud LLM, using step-level RL that jointly optimizes task solving and delegation with fine-grained credit assignment. An external-judge delegation strategy is used to study when to delegate, what context to share and how often to call the cloud model.
w1bB3nAhvd.key_idea: Train the local SLM with step-level RL to decide for itself when to hand a step to the cloud LLM, crediting each delegation decision individually.
w1bB3nAhvd.evidence: Long-horizon agent tasks (keywords mention coding agents) compared with pure-LLM execution; the rest of the abstract is cut off.
w1bB3nAhvd.claimed_gains: Matches or outperforms pure-LLM execution while reducing inference cost by up to 62%.

X1OoGtCMCQ.one_liner: Diagnostic framework, expert-annotated benchmark with calibrated VLM judges, and mitigation probe for hallucinations in GUI agents.
X1OoGtCMCQ.problem: GUI-agent hallucinations span perception and task reasoning under partial observability, and existing benchmarks measure task success, grounding or action fidelity without fine-grained hallucination diagnosis.
X1OoGtCMCQ.method: HalluClear defines GUI-agent hallucination as unsupported belief-action commitment under partial observability with a taxonomy from failure analysis, a three-stage evaluation workflow using an expert-annotated benchmark and qualified VLM judges, and a lightweight structured post-training mitigation probe.
X1OoGtCMCQ.key_idea: Define GUI hallucination as an unsupported belief-action commitment and measure it with credibility-calibrated VLM judges over a failure-derived taxonomy.
X1OoGtCMCQ.evidence: Representative GUI agents on public benchmarks, revealing systematic hallucination patterns across agent families and failure subtypes.

qr6p2Cl8xx.one_liner: Training-free video diffusion speedup coupling sparse attention with hierarchical caching through reciprocal correction and online error feedback.
qr6p2Cl8xx.problem: Composing sparse attention with temporal caching couples their errors, since sparse predictions become the sources for temporal reuse along the sampling trajectory.
qr6p2Cl8xx.method: RECAP uses cached dense refinement to correct omitted interactions in sparse estimates and fresh sparse statistics to track input changes and regulate the aging correction. The corrected predictions then renew the sources for whole-step reuse, coordinated by online error feedback.
qr6p2Cl8xx.key_idea: Share correction information across nearby steps because sparsification errors stay directionally aligned, adapting the correction with online error feedback between dense refreshes.
qr6p2Cl8xx.evidence: Multiple video diffusion models against sparse-attention methods, caching methods and their direct compositions, including HunyuanVideo at 720p for 5-second generation.
qr6p2Cl8xx.claimed_gains: 3.05x speedup on HunyuanVideo at 720p 5-second generation while outperforming all tested direct compositions (the rest is cut off).

qMh25Us5bC.one_liner: Feed-forward 3D scene editing via asymmetric latent inpainting in a unified RGB-geometry latent space from one edited image.
qMh25Us5bC.problem: Existing 3D scene editing relies on per-scene optimization or cascaded edit-and-reconstruct pipelines, causing high test-time cost, limited 3D awareness, and structural inconsistencies.
qMh25Us5bC.method: JointEdit3D adapts a pretrained unified RGB-geometry latent space: given a source video and an edited reference image, it observes only the edited RGB reference latent and jointly generates the remaining RGB latents and the entire geometry latent. A SceneAnchor Branch injects source-scene structure, and edit/background-aware losses balance edited-region fidelity with unedited-content preservation.
qMh25Us5bC.key_idea: Inpaint all remaining RGB latents and the whole geometry latent from only the edited reference latent, with a SceneAnchor Branch injecting source-scene structure.
qMh25Us5bC.evidence: Compared with prior baselines on edited-region quality, 3D structural completeness, and background preservation, using the new SceneEdit3D-15K paired dataset and the 100-sample SceneEdit3D-Bench.

A0CS66R2is.one_liner: Specialises pretrained non-causal generative models into causal mechanisms for chest X-ray counterfactuals using latent flow matching.
A0CS66R2is.problem: Counterfactual image generation is held back in healthcare by scarce annotated data, distribution shift between datasets, and a mismatch between pretrained generative models and those needed for counterfactual inference.
A0CS66R2is.method: They propose specialisation, a data- and parameter-efficient framework for adapting pretrained non-causal generative models into causal mechanisms under distribution shift, and use it to train RadCF with latent flow matching.
A0CS66R2is.key_idea: Specialise a pretrained non-causal generative model into a causal mechanism with data- and parameter-efficient adaptation under distribution shift, using latent flow matching.
A0CS66R2is.evidence: Validated on three chest X-ray datasets with different dataset shifts, data volumes, and counterfactual questions involving highly localised interventions, plus a downstream medical classifier for shortcut detection and mitigation.

uIWcuELv6h.one_liner: Parameter-free accelerated Monteiro-Svaiter-type second-order method for inexact Hessians under generalized smoothness, with backtracking on one regularization parameter.
uIWcuELv6h.problem: Second-order convex optimization is studied when the local Hessian Lipschitz constant can grow linearly with the gradient norm, Hessians are only inexact, and neither the inexactness level nor smoothness constants are known.
uIWcuELv6h.method: They develop adaptive algorithms, including an accelerated Monteiro-Svaiter-type method, whose backtracking adapts a single regularization parameter that jointly captures Hessian inexactness and local smoothness. The resulting rates split into a far-from-solution regime with geometric convergence and a near-solution regime governed by ordinary Hessian smoothness and the inexactness level.
uIWcuELv6h.key_idea: Run backtracking on a single regularization parameter that jointly captures Hessian inexactness and local Hessian smoothness inside an accelerated Monteiro-Svaiter-type method.
uIWcuELv6h.evidence: Theoretical complexity analysis only as stated; the accelerated method's complexity matches the lower bound for second-order methods with delta-inexact Hessians in the classical Lipschitz-Hessian setting, and no experiments are mentioned.

9BavSZeldZ.one_liner: Video world simulation specifying object motion inside a unified spatial-memory world state, independent of camera trajectory.
9BavSZeldZ.problem: Intervening in a world model and observing the consequences from freely chosen viewpoints is hard, because object motion and viewpoint change are ambiguous in the control specification.
9BavSZeldZ.method: UniState uses a unified world-state representation that merges spatial memory and user interventions, so users specify object motion within spatial memory and separately choose the camera trajectory. Training and sampling strategies help generated videos follow the specified motion and camera while still synthesizing extra motion and plausible interactions beyond the prescribed transformations.
9BavSZeldZ.key_idea: Specify object motion inside a shared spatial-memory world state while choosing the camera trajectory independently of it.
9BavSZeldZ.evidence: Experiments comparing joint object and camera control against existing methods, plus qualitative evidence that intervention-induced scene changes persist across rollouts.

uQtvcBeYA0.one_liner: Adds forecast-initialized registry slots inside a video DiT, supervised with future representations, to hold predictive dynamics.
uQtvcBeYA0.problem: Standard video tokens jointly encode appearance and dynamics, so a video generator has no distinct state for learning and reading predictive dynamics needed for physically plausible futures.
uQtvcBeYA0.method: Physical Registry adds temporally grounded registry slots inside a video DiT that are initialized from an observation-conditioned forecast, co-evolve with video tokens, and receive future-representation supervision.
uQtvcBeYA0.key_idea: Add registry slots to the video DiT, initialize them from an observation-conditioned forecast, let them co-evolve with video tokens, and supervise them with future representations.
uQtvcBeYA0.evidence: A controlled comparison of predictive-state interfaces on unseen Physics-IQ scenarios, tests across Cosmos and WAN backbones, and WorldModelBench evaluation on four backbones.
uQtvcBeYA0.claimed_gains: Improves vanilla fine-tuning by 7.8/6.2 points on I2V/V2V on Physics-IQ, and with 0.45% additional parameters Cosmos 3 Nano 16B reaches 43.56, above the published I2V score of 42.7 for Cosmos 3 Super 64B.

olTngqB2XO.one_liner: Transfers pretrained UMA atomistic encoders to total DOS prediction with end-to-end adaptation and a shape-amplitude factorized spectral decoder.
olTngqB2XO.problem: Fast, accurate DOS prediction is hard because the target is a high-dimensional structured spectrum, and existing ML approaches rely on DOS supervision alone without exploiting information in large pretrained atomistic models.
olTngqB2XO.method: UMA-DOS encodes a crystal structure with a pretrained UMA atomistic encoder, aggregates node-level features into a graph-level representation, and maps it to an energy-resolved DOS through a structured spectral decoder with explicit shape-amplitude factorization.
olTngqB2XO.key_idea: Fine-tune a pretrained UMA atomistic encoder end-to-end and decode the DOS through separate shape and amplitude factors.
olTngqB2XO.evidence: A unified Materials Project evaluation pipeline comparing against reproduced baselines, with the clearest advantages in shape-sensitive measures of spectral fidelity.

jrYRhzjMcs.one_liner: Replaces token-wise recirculation with a few rounds of parallel Jacobi fixed-point updates over all token positions.
jrYRhzjMcs.problem: Recirculation feeds deeper-layer token states back to shallower layers, but its token-wise recursion makes processing a known sequence expensive in prompt prefill, evaluation, hyperparameter selection, and training of its auxiliary mixer.
jrYRhzjMcs.method: Jacobi recirculation replaces the recursion with a few rounds of parallel updates over all token positions. They prove the iteration is exact after finitely many rounds, converges geometrically under a local contraction condition, and gives convergent training gradients under extra regularity.
jrYRhzjMcs.key_idea: Update all token positions in parallel for a few Jacobi rounds, a fixed-point iteration that is exact after finitely many rounds and converges geometrically under a contraction condition.
jrYRhzjMcs.evidence: Experiments across model families and sizes show two to three rounds reproduce sequential recirculation even for models never trained for this iteration, and prompt prefill before generation preserves downstream accuracy; supported by convergence proofs.
jrYRhzjMcs.claimed_gains: Speeds up single-sequence prefill by more than an order of magnitude and reduces mixer training from hours to minutes.

3eAEsybp7u.one_liner: Uses a convex congestion potential to characterize equilibria and prove convergence of learning dynamics in continuous-time mean field games.
3eAEsybp7u.problem: The paper studies stationary equilibria and learning dynamics in a finite-state continuous-time mean field game with population-dependent action-completion rates, whose state-action dynamics follow a nonlinear Markov process.
3eAEsybp7u.method: A smooth convex congestion potential makes equilibrium populations correspond one-to-one with optimizers of an Eisenberg-Gale-type convex program, and an equivalent population game over deterministic unichain policies has a concave ordinal potential. They then analyze state-policy dynamics under two revision mechanisms, Poisson-rate opportunities and event-driven opportunities at action completions.
3eAEsybp7u.key_idea: Use the convex potential's Eisenberg-Gale variational structure and a concave ordinal potential to prove convergence of state-action, best-response, and state-policy dynamics.
3eAEsybp7u.evidence: Theoretical results only as stated: global convergence under any fixed unichain policy, convergence of best-response and state-policy dynamics to the policy-equilibrium set, and a small-revision-rate limit; no experiments are mentioned.

U1FXlUnvHG.one_liner: Spectral clipping: clamps layer-wise gradient singular values above a threshold while preserving singular directions.
U1FXlUnvHG.problem: Standard gradient clipping treats parameters as vectors and ignores matrix structure, even though data outliers amplify only a few leading singular values of layer-wise gradient matrices.
U1FXlUnvHG.method: Spectral clipping clamps singular values that exceed a threshold while preserving singular directions, generalizes gradient norm clipping, and plugs into existing optimizers. They add layer-wise adaptive thresholds from moving averages or sliding-window quantiles of top singular values, and clip only the top r singular values with randomized truncated SVD.
U1FXlUnvHG.key_idea: Clamp only the singular values of each layer's gradient matrix that exceed a threshold, keeping singular directions and the rest of the spectrum unchanged.
U1FXlUnvHG.evidence: A convergence analysis for non-convex optimization with spectrally clipped SGD under heavy-tailed noise, plus experiments on synthetic heavy-tailed settings and neural network training tasks.
U1FXlUnvHG.claimed_gains: Optimal O(K^((2-2*alpha)/(3*alpha-2))) convergence rate for spectrally clipped SGD under heavy-tailed noise, with competitive empirical performance but no empirical numbers stated.

xUHg2Gbaoo.one_liner: Shows via preference score and interventions that LMs form answer preferences from question prefixes that bias final Yes/No decisions.
xUHg2Gbaoo.problem: A language model may form an answer preference before a question is complete, and it is unclear whether this early preference causally influences its final decision once the question is complete.
xUHg2Gbaoo.method: In binary Yes/No question answering they introduce a preference score (PS) as a behavioral measure of provisional answer preference, then intervene on question-prefix representations and on question-prefix circuits selected by their contribution to final-answer computation. They also steer against the early preference and suppress those circuits.
xUHg2Gbaoo.key_idea: Measure early answer preference with a preference score, then intervene on question-prefix representations and circuits to test their causal effect on the final answer.
xUHg2Gbaoo.evidence: Four models on binary Yes/No QA: final-answer accuracy is lower when the correct answer conflicts with the early preference, and steering or circuit suppression makes final decisions less likely to follow the initially favored answer.

8KEp2wh2KQ.one_liner: Arbitrary-scale atmospheric super-resolution using grid-node anchors, on-demand adaptive probes within cells, and scale-aware rendering.
8KEp2wh2KQ.problem: Arbitrary-scale super-resolution of atmospheric fields may be limited when models do not account for region-specific detail recovery needs and variation in the target scale.
8KEp2wh2KQ.method: A2PSR treats input grid nodes as stable anchors that preserve basic information and generates probes carrying auxiliary information within grid cells on demand, forming the reference information for reconstruction. Scale-aware rendering then regulates the influence of that reference information to enable continuous-scale reconstruction.
8KEp2wh2KQ.key_idea: Treat grid nodes as anchors, generate adaptive probes inside cells on demand as reference information, and let scale-aware rendering set its influence by target scale.
8KEp2wh2KQ.evidence: Experiments on ERA5 within the 1-2x training scale range and at extrapolation scales including 22.5x, compared with arbitrary-scale methods.
8KEp2wh2KQ.claimed_gains: Performs well within the 1-2x training scale range and outperforms all evaluated arbitrary-scale methods at the tested extrapolation scales, including 22.5x, with no metric values stated.

xvloOO0IWo.one_liner: 4B grounding foundation model emitting points and boxes as quantized-coordinate tokens, trained with spatial pretraining, SFT and GRPO.
xvloOO0IWo.problem: Vision-language-action and world-action models take perception from general-purpose vision-language and video-generation backbones, which still fail at precise grounding in clutter, for tiny objects, and at closed-loop speed.
xvloOO0IWo.method: GroundingPI is a 4B model that generates points and boxes as quantized coordinates in a shared vocabulary. Training combines multimodal and spatial pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning with GRPO, using public datasets and dedicated data engines.
xvloOO0IWo.key_idea: Emit points and boxes as quantized coordinate tokens in the shared vocabulary, trained by multimodal and spatial pretraining, SFT, then GRPO reinforcement learning.
xvloOO0IWo.evidence: Evaluated against 44 baselines across 34 grounding benchmarks spanning 11 perceptual capabilities, and as a visual backbone on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa-GR1, and nuScenes.
xvloOO0IWo.claimed_gains: Averages 73.68% across 34 grounding benchmarks versus 71.54% for the larger GPT-6 Astra, with relative gains up to 24.8% over the strongest baseline on RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa-GR1, and on RoboCasa-GR1 training with 50% of demonstrations beats baselines trained with 75%.

cFeUO2Tf0r.one_liner: Scores synthetic degradations by held-out gain over a budget-matched clean-augmentation control to curate a fixed synthetic budget.
cFeUO2Tf0r.problem: Choosing synthetic degradations for dense prediction needs an estimate of training utility, but the clean-versus-degraded gap can shrink when clean performance worsens, and degraded-only improvement credits progress that clean training would also produce.
cFeUO2Tf0r.method: The controlled Reducible Degradation Gap (cRDG) scores regions (a degradation type plus severity bin) by running two budget-matched probes from a common checkpoint that differ only in one augmentation slot, holding either a synthetic degradation or a clean augmentation. The score is the gain on held-out degraded images relative to the clean-control probe, with clean harm as a separate feasibility constraint, and CuRB ranks feasible regions by cRDG to fill a fixed synthetic budget.
cFeUO2Tf0r.key_idea: Score a degradation region by its gain on held-out degraded images relative to a budget-matched clean-augmentation probe from the same checkpoint, then rank feasible regions by that score.
cFeUO2Tf0r.evidence: The visible abstract is cut off before the results; it states only that cRDG reveals a correctable severity band whose score-weighted centroid moves with the predictor, starting checkpoint, and training budget.

nxy3JoRmeI.one_liner: Streaming feed-forward 3DGS that treats per-pixel Gaussians as candidates, controlling placement, retention and opacity over a Gaussian lifecycle.
nxy3JoRmeI.problem: In streaming feed-forward 3DGS from unposed video, each frame's Gaussians stay fixed as new frames arrive so prediction errors accumulate, and dense per-pixel predictions add redundant Gaussians that degrade long-sequence rendering.
nxy3JoRmeI.method: LifeStreamGS treats dense Gaussian predictions as candidates and controls them through merge-guided Gaussian proposal, existence-aware candidate validation, and view- and time-aware opacity aging. For long videos it uses chunk-wise streaming that reconstructs overlapping windows and aligns them into a shared coordinate system.
nxy3JoRmeI.key_idea: Treat dense per-pixel Gaussian predictions as candidates, then merge-guided proposal, existence-aware validation and view- and time-aware opacity aging control placement, retention and contribution.
nxy3JoRmeI.evidence: Experiments on novel-view synthesis quality, runtime, and GPU memory against optimization-based baselines, plus 500-view reconstruction and online video stabilization.
nxy3JoRmeI.claimed_gains: Competitive novel-view synthesis quality with lower runtime and GPU memory than the evaluated optimization-based baselines in most tested settings, and supports 500-view reconstruction.

5rrS3uswYR.one_liner: Refines segmentation masks by unrolling damped mean-field inference in an image-conditioned CRF over pixel labels and latent regions.
5rrS3uswYR.problem: It is unclear whether the gains of learned mask refiners come from explicit structure or added capacity, and whether they persist across mask generators.
5rrS3uswYR.method: UnfoldCRF casts refinement as inference in a CRF over pixel labels and latent regions, with an energy combining a corrected unary term, learned local pairwise interactions, and image-and-mask-conditioned soft pixel-region associations with mass-normalized consistency over semantic and null region states. Refinement unrolls damped mean-field updates on this shared energy.
5rrS3uswYR.key_idea: Unroll damped mean-field updates on a single CRF energy with corrected unary, learned pairwise, and image-and-mask-conditioned soft pixel-region terms, rather than free learned updates.
5rrS3uswYR.evidence: Compared with matched recurrent refiners, trainable higher-order CRFs, and free-update controls on COD10K and a five-benchmark train-once suite, with frozen refiners applied to SAM3, DSS, and SAM3-Adapter outputs, refined pseudo-labels for downstream training, and joint 19-class refinement on Cityscapes.
5rrS3uswYR.claimed_gains: On COD10K UnfoldCRF-S reaches .745 F-omega-beta with 8.5% of images made worse versus .739 and 10.4% for SPFU and .735 and 11.7% for matched attention; mean delta-IoU is 4.2 points versus 2.0 for its control on the five-benchmark suite, the DINOv2-based variant gains 6.3 points, and Cityscapes mIoU starts from 79.4 (the improved value is cut off).

dj3jCaz82F.one_liner: Harmful SFT leaves a continuous checkpoint-update trace; TRACE scores unknown checkpoints against harmful and non-harmful reference prototypes.
dj3jCaz82F.problem: Safety auditing of post-trained LLMs relies on model behavior, which requires running the model and depends on the coverage of available evaluations.
dj3jCaz82F.method: They define a reference geometry from pure harmful-compliance, safety-targeted, and benign-utility SFT, in which a checkpoint-level coordinate sH tracks the harmful-objective composition. TRACE localizes an unknown checkpoint update relative to frozen harmful and non-harmful reference prototypes and converts this geometry into a continuous harmful-objective score, using weights only.
dj3jCaz82F.key_idea: Locate an unknown checkpoint update relative to frozen harmful and non-harmful reference prototypes in weight-update space and convert the geometry into a continuous harmful-objective score.
dj3jCaz82F.evidence: Four 7-8B backbones with the same ordering persisting at larger scales, plus matched compliance-versus-refusal controls and controls for harmful-example count and generic training intensity.
dj3jCaz82F.claimed_gains: The checkpoint coordinate sH tracks controlled harmful-objective composition with Spearman correlations of 0.986-0.992 across four 7-8B backbones.

tbB3ehqcun.one_liner: Replaces iKFAD's friction tensor with a rank-1 outer product of row and column momentum statistics, cutting memory to O(m+n).
tbB3ehqcun.problem: iKFAD, an adaptive-friction optimizer that performs as well as Adam, carries the same O(mn) per-layer memory overhead as Adam's second-moment buffer.
tbB3ehqcun.method: Rank-1 iKFAD (R-iKFAD) factorizes the friction tensor into a rank-1 outer product built from row and column momentum statistics. They analyze continuous-time dynamics, proving exponential convergence under strong convexity for linear damping and convergence to the minimiser with matching energy bounds at zero damping.
tbB3ehqcun.key_idea: Replace the m-by-n friction tensor with an outer product of row and column momentum statistics, so friction memory is O(m+n) instead of O(mn).
tbB3ehqcun.evidence: Experiments on GPT2-Nano, TinyViT, DistilBERT, and GPT2-S, plus continuous-time convergence proofs in two damping regimes.
tbB3ehqcun.claimed_gains: Reduces friction memory from O(mn) to O(m+n) per layer, roughly halving total optimizer state, while matching or exceeding iKFAD, with no metric values stated.

ZqgBMiO9ro.one_liner: Simulation-free unbalanced Schrödinger bridge solver regressing on conditional bridges of a killed Brownian reference from an optimal endpoint coupling.
ZqgBMiO9ro.problem: Reconstructing stochastic cell dynamics with proliferation and apoptosis from destructive snapshots is hard because growth-based methods do not assign exits and entries to individual cells, and neural solvers for killed diffusion bridges simulate trajectories during training.
ZqgBMiO9ro.method: ELYSIUM jointly learns state transition and mass change, using a killed Brownian reference and its time reversal to build direct regression objectives from an optimal endpoint coupling and conditional bridge distributions. They show the minimizers of the expected objectives recover the optimal unbalanced Schrödinger bridge.
ZqgBMiO9ro.key_idea: Regress directly on conditional bridge distributions of a killed Brownian reference and its time reversal, given an optimal endpoint coupling, jointly learning transition and mass change.
ZqgBMiO9ro.evidence: Simulated data with known killed diffusion dynamics, real single-cell datasets for recovering cell state distributions at unobserved time points and population mass changes, and a proof that the objective's minimizers recover the optimal bridge.

WohX9Le9dD.one_liner: Reward fine-tunes diffusion and flow models by reward-weighting the velocity-matching loss plus an anchor regression term, needing no likelihoods.
WohX9Le9dD.problem: Reward-based fine-tuning of diffusion models inherits likelihood-based policy optimization from LLMs, although diffusion models are trained by velocity regression and do not provide sample likelihoods, forcing approximations via transition likelihoods or ELBOs.
WohX9Le9dD.method: Reward-based velocity matching (RVM) weights the velocity-matching loss by reward and adds an anchor regression term, requiring neither likelihood estimation nor likelihood ratios. It recovers Reinforce Adjoint Matching at the update level, contains DiffusionNFT as a special case, and is closely related to ELBO-based methods.
WohX9Le9dD.key_idea: Weight the velocity-matching loss by reward and add an anchor regression term, avoiding likelihood estimation and likelihood ratios.
WohX9Le9dD.evidence: Text-to-image, text-to-video, and image-to-video generation, including Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, where RVM matches or outperforms the evaluated trajectory-based methods.

i7hKm3rxkL.one_liner: Training-free continual LLM pruning that carries accumulated per-task Hessians across tasks to guide weight selection and reconstruction.
i7hKm3rxkL.problem: Existing continual pruning methods focus on which weights to prune, not on adapting the remaining weights to compensate, and combining accumulated-importance pruning with single-task reconstruction improves final performance but increases forgetting.
i7hKm3rxkL.method: They formulate progressive weight reconstruction that minimizes layer-wise pruning error over all tasks seen so far, and show that under fixed layer inputs and an invertible sum of task Hessians, optimal compensation depends on past tasks only through their accumulated Hessian, so no past calibration data is kept. CARGO carries this curvature across tasks and gates it so directions the task stream stops supporting decay.
i7hKm3rxkL.key_idea: Accumulate per-task Hessians, which suffice for second-order compensation on the joint objective, and gate them so directions the task stream stops supporting decay.
i7hKm3rxkL.evidence: A derivation under fixed layer inputs and an invertible summed Hessian; the experimental results are cut off in the visible abstract.

gLSB9XDZGd.one_liner: Efficient video matting: high-resolution memory matching only in uncertain regions with selected memory, plus a distilled lightweight decoder.
gLSB9XDZGd.problem: Memory-based high-resolution video matting preserves fine detail and temporal consistency, but matching current-frame features against stored memory becomes increasingly costly as resolution grows.
gLSB9XDZGd.method: MatAnyone-E first runs low-resolution propagation to find uncertain regions and the most relevant memory candidates, then performs high-resolution matching only for those regions with the selected memory while reusing low-resolution results elsewhere. A lightweight decoder, designed around measured runtime bottlenecks, is trained to reproduce the original decoder's representations.
gLSB9XDZGd.key_idea: Run low-resolution propagation to find uncertain regions and relevant memory, do high-resolution matching only there, and distill a lightweight decoder from the original decoder's representations.
gLSB9XDZGd.evidence: Comparison with MatAnyone 2 on matting quality, inference speed, and peak GPU memory at 4K; further compiled-inference results are cut off in the visible abstract.
gLSB9XDZGd.claimed_gains: Matting quality comparable to MatAnyone 2 with a 6.1x inference speedup and peak GPU memory reduced to 7.6% of MatAnyone 2 at 4K.

Hrow05Quas.one_liner: Latent-variable reasoning for multimodal embeddings: an input-only prior and an evidence-guided posterior from one MLLM, co-evolved.
Hrow05Quas.problem: Retrieval supervision for embedding models gives pairwise relevance but does not guide the self-generated reasoning used to augment inputs, and existing approaches optimize reasoning conditioned on the input alone, limiting exploration of retrieval-relevant traces.
Hrow05Quas.method: PILOT models reasoning as a latent variable whose prior (conditioned on the input only) and posterior (using extra training-time relational evidence) are distinct reasoning modes of a shared MLLM. An importance-weighted variational objective is instantiated as a prior-posterior co-evolution framework that improves both modes under a shared inference-compatible reward and selectively transfers posterior trajectories.
Hrow05Quas.key_idea: Give the posterior mode extra training-time relational evidence to explore retrieval-relevant reasoning, optimize prior and posterior together with an importance-weighted variational objective, and transfer selected posterior trajectories.
Hrow05Quas.evidence: The visible abstract is cut off before the experiments, so no datasets, baselines, or results are stated.

Pd6IfvSUrd.one_liner: Calibrates per-turn on-policy distillation weights as covariance of signal with return over signal variance, a Fisher-metric projection coefficient.
Pd6IfvSUrd.problem: Existing multi-turn on-policy distillation methods reweight the teacher-matching loss per turn from probability gaps, terminal reward, or a depth schedule, without estimating how teacher supervision at a turn contributes to task success.
Pd6IfvSUrd.method: They view on-policy distillation as a policy-gradient step with a proxy advantage and set each turn's weight to the covariance of the distillation signal with the return divided by the signal variance, which is the projection coefficient of the reward gradient onto the distillation direction in the Fisher metric. The nonnegative parts of the per-turn projections are shown to be the assignment that gains the most reward in the second-order KL geometry of one update.
Pd6IfvSUrd.key_idea: Weight each turn by the covariance of its distillation signal with the return divided by the signal variance, keeping only nonnegative projections.
Pd6IfvSUrd.evidence: The visible abstract is cut off before the instantiation and experiments, so only the derivation is stated.

CQDc2CcjFm.one_liner: Zero-anchored piecewise log-companded KV cache quantizer using mu-law transforms around an exact zero level, with per-layer compander strength.
CQDc2CcjFm.problem: Per-group affine min-max KV cache quantization spreads levels uniformly, yet cache groups have dense zero-centered mass and sparse log-tailed extremes, and query-key logits are residuals of cancelling signed products that are sensitive to small errors near zero.
CQDc2CcjFm.method: μ-Zero applies a monotone μ-law transform separately to the positive and negative sides around an exact zero level, concentrating resolution near zero, preserving asymmetric side extents, and using coarser logarithmic spacing in the tails. A lightweight prefill-time rule picks the compander strength per layer and cache type from scale-free statistics and reuses it during decoding.
CQDc2CcjFm.key_idea: Apply a monotone mu-law transform to positive and negative sides around an exact zero level, concentrating resolution near zero, with compander strength chosen per layer at prefill.
CQDc2CcjFm.evidence: Evaluated across reasoning, code generation, and long-context understanding tasks; the result details are cut off in the visible abstract.

ZTCOyaPEGG.one_liner: Evaluates personal health agents with over 100 Boolean clinical rubrics, activated per query by a context-aware adaptive router.
ZTCOyaPEGG.problem: Open-ended evaluation of personal health agents is bottlenecked because physician annotation is reliable but costly and unscalable, while LLM-as-a-judge evaluators are scalable but subjective, inconsistent, and sometimes clinically misaligned.
ZTCOyaPEGG.method: RubricsTree is an expert-aligned hierarchical taxonomy of over 100 atomic, clinically verifiable Boolean rubrics, evolved from 4,000 real user queries through iterative human-in-the-loop curation with a physician-led expert panel. A context-aware adaptive router activates only the relevant auto-weighted rubric subset for each query.
ZTCOyaPEGG.key_idea: Decompose response quality into over 100 atomic Boolean clinical rubrics and activate only a context-relevant, auto-weighted subset per query via a router.
