ZTCOyaPEGG.evidence: A meta-evaluation showing higher expert alignment than a strong large-scale evaluation baseline on challenging open-ended queries and reliable penalization of contextually degraded responses, plus use as instructions, text feedback, or training rewards on HealthBench with Gemini, GPT, and Qwen models.
ZTCOyaPEGG.claimed_gains: Up to approximately 66% relative gains on HealthBench when used as structured instructions, text feedback, or training rewards.

jJNpDOM1zO.one_liner: Forecasts scene and hand 3D point trajectories jointly, then retargets predicted hand motion to robot actions, enabling human-video pretraining.
jJNpDOM1zO.problem: Existing world action models represent the world as RGB frames or latents and actions as end-effector poses or joint angles, which struggle to capture the 3D spatial structure and contact geometry central to dexterous manipulation.
jJNpDOM1zO.method: PointWAM decomposes the world into a scene and hands and jointly forecasts both as 3D point trajectories in a shared space-time coordinate frame. Given a colored point cloud and a language instruction it predicts how scene and hands co-evolve, then retargets the forecast hand motion to robot actions, and the explicit representation allows pretraining on large-scale human demonstration videos without task-specific object or keypoint selection.
jJNpDOM1zO.key_idea: Represent scene and hands as 3D point trajectories in one space-time frame, forecast both jointly, and retarget the forecast hand motion to robot actions.
jJNpDOM1zO.evidence: Ten DexJoCo tasks against the prior best multi-task success rate, and real-robot single-arm and bimanual tasks against GR00T N1.6 and π0.5.
jJNpDOM1zO.claimed_gains: Surpasses the prior best average multi-task success rate by 11.7 percentage points on ten DexJoCo tasks, with scene-trajectory supervision contributing 10.9 points and human-data pre-training 56.9 points, and outperforms GR00T N1.6 and π0.5 on a real robot (margin cut off).

lV7pRN0I87.one_liner: Generates slide and poster code via RL on decoupled rewards: deterministic verifiers plus a VLM judge with Visual Graph Rubrics.
lV7pRN0I87.problem: Code models cannot see how layout and color choices combine on the canvas, limiting spatial planning and aesthetic quality, while image generators design well but misrender requested content and so are unreliable targets for direct reproduction.
lV7pRN0I87.method: AesCode generates code grounded in the content prompt, using an image generated from the same prompt as aesthetic guidance, and represents the target as a design graph that makes each canvas property attributable. Deterministic verifiers score properties parsable from code and rendering, a VLM judge scores the rest with a sample-specific Visual Graph Rubric, and the decoupled rewards are optimized with RL using per-channel normalization.
lV7pRN0I87.key_idea: Represent the target as a design graph, score code-parsable properties with deterministic verifiers and others with a graph-tied VLM rubric, and normalize each reward channel in RL.
lV7pRN0I87.evidence: A new benchmark that scores verifiable correctness and visual quality separately, with visual scores reported as highly consistent with human judgments; the main results are cut off in the visible abstract.

omATtr3hqv.one_liner: On-policy distillation that adds teacher's log-probability shifts under reflection-conditioned context on student failures as bounded corrective token-level supervision.
omATtr3hqv.problem: Standard on-policy distillation relies on prefix-conditioned teacher predictions and does not incorporate the teacher's retrospective diagnosis of why a completed reasoning attempt failed.
omATtr3hqv.method: For verifier-identified failures, RC-OPD has a frozen teacher write reflective feedback and score the same response under standard and reflection-conditioned contexts, using token-level log-probability differences as corrective signal on diagnosed reasoning suffixes. The combined distillation signal is bounded and integrated with outcome-based reinforcement learning.
omATtr3hqv.key_idea: Add the teacher's token-level log-probability change between standard and reflection-conditioned contexts to base OPD on diagnosed failure suffixes, with the combined signal bounded.
omATtr3hqv.evidence: The visible abstract is cut off before the experiments, so no datasets, models, or results are stated.

DE4A5wOA0k.one_liner: Sparse attention that replaces the unread KV tail with a few error-guided cluster proxies using count-aware mean tokens.
DE4A5wOA0k.problem: Sparse attention reads only a small subset of the KV cache, and discarding the unread tail biases the output while sampling it fails at reads of 5% and below, where the tail likely holds heavy hitters the selector missed.
DE4A5wOA0k.method: OpenAttention is a pipeline of clustering, ErrorGate, and top-k selection followed by a count-aware mean proxy, using training-free Query-Geometry Clustering (QGC) and a Query-Geometry Selector (QGS) that compress keys while respecting query directions. ErrorGate allocates the exact read across clusters by each cluster's estimated weight error rather than ranking by centroid alone.
DE4A5wOA0k.key_idea: Cluster keys by query geometry, allocate the exact read across clusters by estimated weight error, and summarize each remaining cluster with a count-aware mean proxy token.
DE4A5wOA0k.evidence: A closed-form analysis showing that at low reads sampling nearly doubles the weight error of discarding while a single proxy stays below it, and experiments on RULER-32K HARD with Llama-3.1-8B.
DE4A5wOA0k.claimed_gains: Retains 99% of dense accuracy at a 1% read on RULER-32K HARD with Llama-3.1-8B (further results cut off).

LxcRUHhSTl.one_liner: Depth up-scaling with head-wise memory: distinct product-key retrieval spaces per attention head and shared value storage with head-specific projections.
LxcRUHhSTl.problem: Depth Up-Scaling duplicates FFN-heavy blocks, raising parameter count and dense per-token computation, while sparse retrieval can decouple capacity from compute but must avoid large memory overhead and preserve the heterogeneous representations of individual attention heads.
LxcRUHhSTl.method: MIDUS organizes memory around attention heads, using distinct product-key spaces per head and shared value storage with head-specific projections. They show that under common retrieval weights shared value realization incurs a loss gap when heads need different outputs, and that MIDUS recovers the independent optimum under a shared factorization.
LxcRUHhSTl.key_idea: Give each attention head its own product-key space for retrieval while sharing one value store through head-specific projections.
LxcRUHhSTl.evidence: Llama-3.1-8B experiments against strong DUS baselines including OpT-DeUS, plus a head-importance analysis and a theoretical loss-gap argument.
LxcRUHhSTl.claimed_gains: On Llama-3.1-8B, MIDUS uses 8.3x fewer trainable parameters and 42% less peak training GPU memory than OpT-DeUS with higher generation throughput, while remaining competitive with strong DUS baselines.

XFg3wEzJXQ.one_liner: ADMM framework for joint LLM sparsification and quantization with a closed-form joint projection onto sparse support and quantization grid.
XFg3wEzJXQ.problem: Sparsification and quantization of LLMs are usually optimized independently, overlooking their interactions and giving suboptimal compression trade-offs.
XFg3wEzJXQ.method: ASQ is an ADMM-based framework that optimizes sparsification and quantization jointly under one formulation with convergence guarantees. Its exact closed-form joint projection resolves sparse support and quantized values together, accounting for each weight's importance to the objective and its representability on the quantization grid.
XFg3wEzJXQ.key_idea: ADMM updates whose closed-form joint projection picks sparse support and quantized values together, weighing weight importance and quantization-grid representability.
XFg3wEzJXQ.evidence: Multiple model architectures and scales under aggressive compression, with the gap to joint-compression baselines widening at extreme sparsity and low bit-widths, plus hardware-compatible 2:4 sparsity with INT4 on Qwen3-8B-Base.
XFg3wEzJXQ.claimed_gains: Under 2:4 sparsity with INT4 on Qwen3-8B-Base, a 4.78x memory reduction and up to 3.20x end-to-end decode speedup relative to dense BF16 inference.

fWzACWbDEq.one_liner: Injects projected pretrained-encoder representations into a diffusion transformer as a temporary scaffold that is progressively internalized during training.
fWzACWbDEq.problem: REPA aligns projections of diffusion transformer hidden states to pretrained encoder representations, but the encoder representations themselves do not take part in the denoising process.
fWzACWbDEq.method: REPresentation Injection (REPI) is a training framework in which projected encoder representations are injected into the diffusion transformer, first as a temporary scaffold and then progressively internalized, and it can be combined with REPA.
fWzACWbDEq.key_idea: Inject projected encoder representations into the diffusion transformer as a temporary scaffold that is progressively internalized, reversing REPA's projection direction.
fWzACWbDEq.evidence: Experiments across a wide range of backbones comparing REPI, REPA, and their combination, including a comparison with vanilla SiT trained for 7M steps.
fWzACWbDEq.claimed_gains: REPI outperforms REPA across backbones, and with only 160K training steps REPI + REPA surpasses vanilla SiT trained for 7M steps, a speedup of over 43.5x.

wYPJstPLqi.one_liner: Egocentric world model conditioned on interaction and egomotion latent actions learned by pixel-space motion factorization with limited mask supervision.
wYPJstPLqi.problem: Egocentric world models mostly focus on egomotion control because densely annotated interaction videos are scarce, and latent action models entangle object interaction and egomotion in a single representation.
wYPJstPLqi.method: MoFA-LAM pretrains region-level latent actions through pixel-space motion factorization and aggregates them into interaction and egomotion representations via region-specific reconstruction with limited mask supervision. MoFA-World is an egocentric world model conditioned on these two representations through distinct pathways.
wYPJstPLqi.key_idea: Pretrain region-level latent actions by pixel-space motion factorization, then aggregate them by region-specific reconstruction into separate interaction and egomotion representations conditioning the world model through distinct pathways.
wYPJstPLqi.evidence: Probing experiments showing functional specialization of the two representations and the benefit of motion-factorized over vanilla LAM pretraining, plus demonstrations of cross-scene action transfer and adaptation to dataset-specific controls.

bIeaWL947E.one_liner: Benchmark of 8K synthetic household value-conflict scenarios with images and multiple robot actions, each prioritizing a different human value.
bIeaWL947E.problem: Household robots are evaluated on task completion, but no benchmark tests which actions they choose when human values such as autonomy, efficiency, or social appropriateness conflict.
bIeaWL947E.method: RobotValues contains 8K scenarios, each a realistic synthetically generated household image with multiple plausible robot actions that prioritize different values. It is built through LLM-assisted scenario generation, stakeholder-grounded value extraction, image generation, and automatic quality control.
bIeaWL947E.key_idea: Pair each generated household image with plausible robot actions that each prioritize a different human value, then test default preferences and steerability across VLMs.
bIeaWL947E.evidence: Ten VLMs used in robotics were evaluated, showing default value preferences such as safety and accommodation and underselection of privacy-prioritizing actions.
bIeaWL947E.claimed_gains: Benchmark finding: models pick incorrect actions 80% of the time on average when prompted to prioritize values that conflict with their defaults.

Q0R1yHb9VM.one_liner: Multi-turn VLM agent for room re-identification choosing per turn to commit, verify geometrically, or inspect semantically.
Q0R1yHb9VM.problem: Room re-identification pipelines run every query through a rigid cascade of evidence extractors, wasting computation on already-resolved queries and sometimes overturning correct decisions with noisy later evidence.
Q0R1yHb9VM.method: Roomer decides each turn whether to commit, verify candidates geometrically, or inspect them semantically. Sight-OPSD trains a 4B raw-image Inspector using training-only regional and geometric teaching views, and the Router is trained with multi-turn group-relative credit assignment using Outcome Credit, Commitment Credit for when to stop, and Probe Credit based on evidence displacement.
Q0R1yHb9VM.key_idea: Train the Inspector by privileged on-policy self-distillation (what to see) and the Router with outcome, commitment, and probe credits (when to stop and which probes help).
Q0R1yHb9VM.evidence: The visible abstract is cut off before the experiments, so no datasets, baselines, or results are stated.

uj9KkeqyWK.one_liner: Space Syntax Integration Operator recovers convex-space access graphs to evaluate floorplans and drive RL post-training of diffusion generators.
uj9KkeqyWK.problem: Fidelity objectives inherited from visual and geometric generators do not capture how spaces should be organized for use in floorplans, and this organization stays implicit in generated representations, limiting direct evaluation and feedback.
uj9KkeqyWK.method: The Space Syntax Integration Operator (SSIO) recovers convex-space access graphs across heterogeneous formats as a shared design container, which supports the RPLAN-SSI benchmark measuring functional-profile alignment (IPD) and within-plan public-space advantage (PIAD). Space Syntax-Guided Post-Training (SSPT) then serves as a plug-and-play design-learning interface for improving generators.
uj9KkeqyWK.key_idea: Recover convex-space access graphs with the Space Syntax Integration Operator, then use their integration measures for population-level evaluation and as feedback in RL post-training.
uj9KkeqyWK.evidence: SSIO applied to four residential corpora spanning 15 countries, a comparison showing generated floorplans give public spaces a smaller integration advantage, and SSPT applied to five heterogeneous diffusion generators.

U847Bdm5Hr.one_liner: Generates limit order book messages by selecting a resting order first, then masking invalid fields, guaranteeing replayability.
U847Bdm5Hr.problem: Existing LOB message generators can emit raw messages inconsistent with the current market state, forcing post-hoc correction or rejection and resampling that distort the message distribution or raise inference cost.
U847Bdm5Hr.method: ReLOBGen first samples the referenced order from a learned distribution over eligible resting orders, computed from cached order representations and a context-dependent query. It then generates the remaining message fields with invalid tokens masked out so they stay consistent with that order and the market state.
U847Bdm5Hr.key_idea: Select the referenced resting order first from a learned eligible-order distribution, then mask invalid tokens so all other fields stay consistent with it.
U847Bdm5Hr.evidence: 500-message rollouts compared against the LOBS5 baseline on replayability, market-realism statistics, and per-message speed.
U847Bdm5Hr.claimed_gains: 100% replayability in 500-message rollouts, improved market realism (top-of-book statistics, relative prices of LOB messages), and a 2.7-3.6x speedup per replayed message over LOBS5.

EZIiWzX6tO.one_liner: Non-parametric framework that distills interaction experience into action preconditions and effects over factorized world states for MLLM embodied planning.
EZIiWzX6tO.problem: MLLM planners do not fully capture environment-dependent action preconditions and effects, and existing adaptation either needs costly environment-specific training or relies on unstructured experience that is hard to ground and reuse.
EZIiWzX6tO.method: CausGround identifies action preconditions and effects from interaction experience and stores them in a factorized world-state representation covering object attributes and inter-object relations. At planning time it grounds task-relevant causal dependencies in the current observation for backward reasoning over preconditions and forward reasoning over effects.
EZIiWzX6tO.key_idea: Store experience as action-centered causal knowledge (preconditions and effects) over factorized object-attribute and relation states, and ground it in the current observation for backward and forward planning.
EZIiWzX6tO.evidence: Evaluated on long-horizon embodied settings spanning simulated high-level planning and interaction reasoning; the abstract is truncated after that point.

fLokQOXhRl.one_liner: Benchmark of 64 SEM/EBSD microstructure-analysis instances testing agents on observe, model, measure, and reason steps.
fLokQOXhRl.problem: Existing benchmarks focus on knowledge-centric or single-step tasks and cover little of end-to-end microstructural characterization in realistic experimental settings.
fLokQOXhRl.method: Built from controlled laboratory experiments, it has 64 instances on SEM and EBSD data across four tasks: static defect-state, temporal defect-evolution, inter-grain structure, and intra-grain orientation-variation analysis. Each task requires agents to produce spatial evidence, executable code, numerical results, and scientific conclusions.
fLokQOXhRl.key_idea: Score agents per capability (Observe, Model, Measure, Reason) on long-horizon analyses over experimentally acquired data, with multiple interdependent outputs per instance.
fLokQOXhRl.evidence: Evaluates 15 frontier models under a fixed execution harness and further compares six more systems; the abstract is truncated before saying what they are.

wLBTz52smW.one_liner: Detects jailbreaks by comparing prediction errors of benign versus jailbreak conditional Koopman models of hidden-state evolution.
wLBTz52smW.problem: Hidden-state jailbreak detectors do not explicitly model transition relationships, so unseen attacks with unfamiliar trajectories are poorly covered even though their transitions share predictive regularities with known jailbreaks.
wLBTz52smW.method: CORD learns benign and jailbreak dynamical models through a conditional Koopman formulation with shared observables over token progression and network depth. Both models predict the same observed successors, and the residual contrast gives higher risk when jailbreak dynamics explain the evolution better than benign dynamics.
wLBTz52smW.key_idea: Score risk by the difference between benign and jailbreak Koopman-model prediction residuals on the same observed hidden-state transitions.
wLBTz52smW.evidence: The abstract states extensive experiments but is truncated before naming datasets, models, or results.

Ki6897T7x6.one_liner: Solves semi-discrete optimal transport by layering target points nearest-to-farthest and warm-starting each layer from solved neighbors.
Ki6897T7x6.problem: Monte Carlo geometric variational solvers for semi-discrete optimal transport use a global cold-start synchronous iteration whose partitioning cost rises sharply as target points scale up.
Ki6897T7x6.method: Target points are partitioned layer by layer from nearest to farthest, and head and tail layers form a global skeleton that fixes the Power diagram topology in advance. Each point in a newly added layer is initialized with the Brenier height of its nearest solved neighbor, then refined with warm starts.
Ki6897T7x6.key_idea: Fix the Power diagram skeleton from head and tail layers, then add layers incrementally with Brenier heights initialized from the nearest solved neighbor.
Ki6897T7x6.evidence: Experiments on standard and complex real-world distributions, plus supplementary tests on generative modeling, adversarial attacks, and out-of-distribution overconfidence.
Ki6897T7x6.claimed_gains: An average 53.88% acceleration versus the original MC solver with permille-scale error against ground-truth Brenier heights, and only negligible percentage-to-permille deviations in downstream tasks.

5wn2X8MqAi.one_liner: Flow-matching defocus deblurring trained with reblurring feedback from a learned circle-of-confusion map to correct latent endpoints.
5wn2X8MqAi.problem: Flow Matching restoration produces plausible results but can hallucinate details that are not supported by the observed defocus blur.
5wn2X8MqAi.method: FCFlow learns a spatially varying circle-of-confusion (CoC) map from the blurred input without depth or CoC annotations. At a sampled flow time, the predicted velocity gives a sharp endpoint proposal by single-step extrapolation, which is decoded, reblurred with the CoC map, and the discrepancy becomes a bounded latent endpoint correction; this branch is dropped at inference.
5wn2X8MqAi.key_idea: Reblur the decoded one-step endpoint proposal with the estimated CoC map and convert the discrepancy with the input into a bounded latent endpoint correction during training.
5wn2X8MqAi.evidence: Experiments on DPDD, LFDOF, and RealDOF; the abstract is truncated before the results.

1jHvHdCBTm.one_liner: Tree-structured multi-agent search where specialized LLM agents evolve molecules along separate branches for multi-objective optimization.
1jHvHdCBTm.problem: Optimizing molecules within a single evolving search context entangles conflicting objectives and discards the path-specific experience needed to reach distinct Pareto regions.
1jHvHdCBTm.method: ATOM treats alternative optimization trajectories as the units of Pareto exploration and places specialized agents on different tree branches, each evolving molecules toward one objective while accumulating trajectory-specific structural experience. Three coordination mechanisms at lateral, hierarchical, and global scales share knowledge across paths.
1jHvHdCBTm.key_idea: Organize agents along tree branches so each accumulates trajectory-specific experience for one objective, with lateral, hierarchical, and global knowledge sharing across paths.
1jHvHdCBTm.evidence: Molecular optimization benchmarks involving predicted bioactivity, synthetic accessibility, and CYP3A4 inhibition.
1jHvHdCBTm.claimed_gains: Attains the best mean aggregate hypervolume and competitive results on the remaining measures; the abstract is truncated and gives no numbers.

VcDGTJqzEp.one_liner: Attentive probe for frozen ECG encoders with four queries anchored to P, QRS, ST, T phases of each beat.
VcDGTJqzEp.problem: ECG diagnosis models degrade across hospitals, and mean pooling of frozen-encoder tokens dilutes beat-locked diagnostic information while a plain multi-query attentive probe leaves its queries unassigned.
VcDGTJqzEp.method: BAP expands one R-peak per beat into attention targets for the P, QRS, ST, and T phases. A training-only alignment loss allocates each query over every beat and registers it to one phase, while the diagnostic loss decides what the query reads; the encoder stays frozen.
VcDGTJqzEp.key_idea: Use training-only R-peak-derived phase targets and an alignment loss to bind each probe query to one beat phase across every beat.
VcDGTJqzEp.evidence: Phase-resolved probing of frozen tokens and cross-site transfer on four encoders, with phase roles checked across training seeds and on an external benchmark; the abstract is truncated after mentioning a release.
VcDGTJqzEp.claimed_gains: Highest mean transfer among the compared probes and improvement over the linear probe on all four encoders, with the largest gains on diagnoses that mean pooling dilutes; no numeric values are stated.

EPmnNAtDjE.one_liner: Unified Wasserstein-gradient-flow view of distributional training, yielding MGFlow, which matches Gaussian-mixture feature distributions for one-step generation.
EPmnNAtDjE.problem: Distributional training for one-step generation lacks a unified theory separating distribution modeling from the matching discrepancy, and mixture expressivity alone does not resolve mode collapse.
EPmnNAtDjE.method: A framework links global objectives to pointwise feature updates via Wasserstein gradient flow and recovers FD-Loss and Gaussian-kernel Drifting as special cases. MGFlow models feature distributions as Gaussian mixtures at adjustable granularity, supports optimal-transport and score-based matching, and couples mass-constrained sample assignment with paired component updates.
EPmnNAtDjE.key_idea: Model frozen-space feature distributions as adjustable-granularity Gaussian mixtures and couple mass-constrained sample assignment with paired component updates to prevent mode collapse.
EPmnNAtDjE.evidence: ImageNet 256x256 with pMF-H and JiT-H, and text-to-image post-training of FLUX.2 [klein] 4B evaluated on GenEval and PickScore.
EPmnNAtDjE.claimed_gains: 1.45 FDr^6 on pMF-H and 1.64 on JiT-H on ImageNet 256x256, surpassing the FD-Loss baseline; the one-step FLUX.2 [klein] 4B outperforms the original four-step model on GenEval and PickScore.

BaVyRkeWRM.one_liner: Inference-time module shifts near-zero MLP activations outward to mimic the reasoning gains from prepending meaningless tokens.
BaVyRkeWRM.problem: Prepending long sequences of meaningless tokens consistently improves LLM reasoning for unexplained reasons, and doing so is an unprincipled way to obtain the effect.
BaVyRkeWRM.method: The authors trace the gains to a redistribution of MLP activations, with fewer near-zero and more large-magnitude values. They propose ARM, which adaptively shifts near-zero post-nonlinearity activations outward at inference without altering the input sequence.
BaVyRkeWRM.key_idea: Adaptively push near-zero post-nonlinearity MLP activations outward at inference to reproduce the activation redistribution caused by meaningless prefix tokens.
BaVyRkeWRM.evidence: An analysis of MLP activations under meaningless-token prefixes, and experiments across diverse benchmarks and model architectures that the abstract does not name.
BaVyRkeWRM.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only says reasoning performance improves consistently with minimal implementation overhead.

7e7wgopS4f.one_liner: Adjoint-equation analysis giving vocabulary-size-independent convergence guarantees for discrete diffusion in any integral probability metric.
7e7wgopS4f.problem: KL-based convergence analyses of discrete diffusion diverge under singular priors such as the masked distribution, and TV bounds depend on vocabulary size S and become vacuous for large vocabularies.
7e7wgopS4f.method: A unified framework works in the space of observables via adjoint equations rather than probability measures, with a regularity analysis for any IPM, a coupling argument for uniform transitions, and score-marginal cancellation and exit-routing techniques for masked transitions. It relies on a single standard rate-matrix regularity assumption.
7e7wgopS4f.key_idea: Analyze discrete diffusion through adjoint equations on observables instead of probability measures, which yields IPM bounds free of vocabulary size for both uniform and masked transitions.
7e7wgopS4f.evidence: Theoretical analysis under one rate-matrix regularity assumption; the visible abstract states no experiments.
7e7wgopS4f.claimed_gains: Convergence bounds that are free of vocabulary size S for both masked and uniform priors in any IPM; no numeric gains are stated.

zU9US3qBih.one_liner: Conjunctive dual-key backdoor for vision-language models, using a ReLU-gated visual adapter and contrastive loss so only image-plus-question triggers it.
zU9US3qBih.problem: Existing multimodal backdoors degenerate into single-modality shortcuts and disrupt task utility, so they cannot require a visual cue and a question to co-occur.
zU9US3qBih.method: GenLock combines a ReLU-gated visual adapter for single-key suppression with a Dual-Key Interaction Contrastive Loss (DKICL) for prefix-conditioned continuation control. Payload-Utility Decoupled Training balances supervision between long payloads and task answers.
zU9US3qBih.key_idea: Gate the visual adapter with ReLU to suppress single-key activation, and add a payload-prefix-conditioned contrastive loss so continuation requires both keys.
zU9US3qBih.evidence: Five LVLM backends, including LLaVA-1.5, with analysis of joint activation and single-key leakage; the abstract is truncated after mentioning the highest score.
zU9US3qBih.claimed_gains: Only approach keeping over 90% selectivity at near-clean utility across five backends; on LLaVA-1.5 joint activation reaches 100.00% with worst-single-key leakage of 0.33%, and DKICL cuts worst-single-key leakage from 83.92% to 0.42%.

ovcl6QPROl.one_liner: Small domain-specific language model for floor-layout generation, trained with DSL tokenization, SFT, and RL on human-preference and verifiable rewards.
ovcl6QPROl.problem: General-purpose foundation models handle structured engineering representations such as architectural layouts poorly.
ovcl6QPROl.method: FLOORA combines a token-efficient DSL, custom tokenization, domain-specific pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning with learned human-preference and verifiable rewards. It is released as a family of small models, with a 0.6B model reported.
ovcl6QPROl.key_idea: Post-train a small layout-DSL model with RL that combines learned human-preference rewards and verifiable rewards, after domain pretraining and SFT.
ovcl6QPROl.evidence: VLM-judge win rates against larger frontier models on out-of-distribution real-world and synthetic buildings, human evaluations, and ablation studies.
ovcl6QPROl.claimed_gains: The 0.6B model reaches VLM-judge win rates up to 96.1% on out-of-distribution real-world buildings and 98.5% on synthetic buildings, and is selected best in 89.3% of human evaluations.

VYee7ydZt9.one_liner: On-policy distillation for flow-matching image models: student queries expert velocity fields on its own rollout states with velocity MSE.
VYee7ydZt9.problem: Text-to-image, local editing, and global editing capabilities conflict when trained into one model: editing degrades T2I, and global and local editing interfere with each other.
VYee7ydZt9.method: DanceOPD routes each sample to one capability field, queries one low-noise student-induced state, and trains with a velocity MSE objective. Each capability source is a velocity field over the shared flow state space, and operator-defined fields such as classifier-free guidance can be absorbed the same way.
VYee7ydZt9.key_idea: Distill expert velocity fields evaluated on the student's own rollout states, routing each sample to one capability field with a plain velocity MSE loss.
VYee7ydZt9.evidence: Experiments on T2I, editing, realism-field absorption, and CFG absorption; the abstract names no models or metrics.

IkYmTAyPXZ.one_liner: Shows recursive self-improvement erodes tail and recovery capabilities in embodied policies, and proposes RESCUE to retain mastered modes.
IkYmTAyPXZ.problem: Under a fixed task distribution, recursive self-improvement can erode tail and error-recovery capabilities while nominal success keeps rising, a failure the authors call silent erosion.
IkYmTAyPXZ.method: A dynamical model over behavior modes identifies two causes: selection, which down-weights poorly performed modes, and visitation drift, which removes post-failure states where recovery is exercised. RESCUE spends a fixed external budget on mastered modes with shrinking data mass, retains them across generations, and forecasts degradation from their coverage.
IkYmTAyPXZ.key_idea: Spend a fixed external data budget on mastered behavior modes whose data mass is shrinking, retain them across generations, and forecast degradation from their coverage.
IkYmTAyPXZ.evidence: Experiments separate data recursion from parameter drift, intervene on each mechanism, and replicate across policy architectures, benchmarks, and real-robot deployment.

J2LwUWQ4LN.one_liner: Highlight detection with separate visual and audio temporal encoders fused by time-varying routing weights, optionally query-conditioned.
J2LwUWQ4LN.problem: Multimodal highlight detection methods focus on how modalities are fused, often before modeling their distinct temporal characteristics.
J2LwUWQ4LN.method: Independently parameterized visual and audio temporal representations are learned first, then combined with time-varying routing weights that can be conditioned on a semantic query.
J2LwUWQ4LN.key_idea: Model each modality with its own temporal parameters before fusion, then mix them with time-varying routing weights instead of fixed fusion.
J2LwUWQ4LN.evidence: Four benchmarks spanning long-form sports broadcasts and web video, ablations of modality-specific versus shared modeling and adaptive versus fixed fusion, and representation analyses.
J2LwUWQ4LN.claimed_gains: Improves over the strongest baseline by up to 6.9 mAP on long-form sports highlight detection, with 1.56 GFLOPs versus 1.93 and 6.49M parameters.

vRn4HkiKwW.one_liner: 500-hour synchronized egocentric human visual-tactile dataset collected with one sensing pipeline, tested on tactile prediction, representation learning, and manipulation.
vRn4HkiKwW.problem: Synchronized tactile data is far scarcer than human video, and the largest visual-tactile resources mix sensors or annotation procedures, so hundreds of hours from one consistent pipeline are rare.
vRn4HkiKwW.method: TouchScale has 500 hours of contact-rich interaction across about 2K predefined task descriptions, with time-aligned egocentric RGB-D, bilateral wrist RGB, and tactile measurements in each recording. The authors study what scale unlocks via cross-dataset generalization, transferable representation learning, and robotic manipulation.
vRn4HkiKwW.key_idea: Collect all 500 hours with one consistent visual-tactile sensing pipeline so scale effects can be measured without sensor or annotation confounds.
vRn4HkiKwW.evidence: Zero-shot cross-dataset tests against EgoTouch on EgoTactile, action-recognition transfer, and robotic manipulation; the abstract is truncated before the manipulation results.
vRn4HkiKwW.claimed_gains: Training on TouchScale instead of EgoTouch improves zero-shot cIoU on EgoTactile by 35.1%, and pretraining on TouchScale improves downstream action recognition accuracy by 49.3%.

cheV6qQzcv.one_liner: RL framework for wide-search agents that derives turn-level credit from changes in verifiable intermediate table states.
cheV6qQzcv.problem: RLVR assigns credit to an entire trajectory, so wide-search agents cannot identify the few decisions that matter in long interactions, and existing systems rely on designed multi-agent setups.
cheV6qQzcv.method: VISTA makes search progress explicit as intermediate table states that track accumulated discoveries, uses changes across consecutive states to attribute credit to the responsible turns, and keeps the terminal outcome as the dominant learning signal.
cheV6qQzcv.key_idea: Track accumulated discoveries in an intermediate table state and assign each turn credit from the change in that state, while keeping the outcome reward as the main signal.
cheV6qQzcv.evidence: Six benchmarks and six models from 4B to 27B, compared against outcome-only GRPO and step-wise RL baselines, with generalization to multi-hop QA benchmarks.
cheV6qQzcv.claimed_gains: On WideSearch, VISTA improves Item F1 by 13.84% relative over outcome-only GRPO on Qwen3-4B, with consistent gains across other model families and scales.

qUCEic0mdh.one_liner: World-action model for photography cascading a video expert with an action expert to predict future views and camera motion.
qUCEic0mdh.problem: Existing autonomous photography methods choose camera actions without modeling their visual outcome, so they cannot reason about how camera motion affects photographic quality.
qUCEic0mdh.method: CamWAM cascades a video expert with an action expert through a lightweight adapter and uses a three-stage video-action learning strategy to align visual evolution with camera motion. Training trajectories come from reversing videos synthesized from curated high-quality photographs.
qUCEic0mdh.key_idea: Feed the video expert's predicted future visual evolution into an action expert through a lightweight adapter to predict continuous camera motions.
qUCEic0mdh.evidence: Extensive experiments that the abstract does not detail, plus cross-domain evaluation in independently constructed 3D Gaussian Splatting environments.

9V4bHxQRc4.one_liner: Identifies a three-dimensional linear subspace in MLLM activations encoding object coordinates, used to read, intervene on, and diagnose spatial reasoning.
9V4bHxQRc4.problem: The internal mechanisms behind spatial reasoning in multimodal language models remain poorly understood.
9V4bHxQRc4.method: Axes are found by differentiating spatial-answer scores with respect to object-token activations, giving horizontal, vertical, and distance coordinates. The authors test readout, viewpoint transformation, and causal interventions, then use direction-word readouts to diagnose spatial reasoning failures.
9V4bHxQRc4.key_idea: Differentiate spatial-answer scores with respect to object-token activations to find a linear subspace whose axes encode horizontal, vertical, and distance coordinates.
9V4bHxQRc4.evidence: Readout under non-spatial questions, causal interventions that alter spatial judgments while largely preserving non-spatial responses, and case studies; no models or numbers are visible in the truncated abstract.

kEggqPr5Wc.one_liner: Shows on-policy distillation gains come from suppressing low log-probability tokens, then proposes teacher-free OPSA with entropy-adaptive negative advantages.
kEggqPr5Wc.problem: In on-policy distillation the teacher scores student trajectories that are off-policy for it, so the reliability of its supervision and the source of the student's improvement are unclear.
kEggqPr5Wc.method: The authors quantify teacher noise (which grows with teacher scale), find the student insensitive to it, and find that a single fixed negative advantage matches teacher-provided ones. OPSA assigns stronger negative signals to high-entropy positions, suppressing tail tokens and redistributing probability mass evenly among head tokens.
kEggqPr5Wc.key_idea: Apply entropy-adaptive negative advantages that push down tail tokens at high-entropy positions and spread mass over head tokens, with no teacher.
kEggqPr5Wc.evidence: Analysis of teacher supervision noise during OPD, and OPSA compared with base Qwen3-1.7B on Avg@32 for AIME24; the abstract is truncated after that.
kEggqPr5Wc.claimed_gains: Compared with the base Qwen3-1.7B, OPSA improves Avg@32 by 35.41 points on AIME24; the abstract is truncated after this.

umJRkn3B4L.one_liner: Prediction-powered quantile learning: synthetic labels estimate pinball risk, trusted data corrects bias, final conformalization improves conditional coverage.
umJRkn3B4L.problem: Post-hoc calibration data may be too limited to learn how uncertainty varies across inputs, while cheap synthetic labels from domain models or LLMs are abundant.
umJRkn3B4L.method: A large synthetic-labeled sample estimates pinball risk, a paired trusted sample corrects its bias, and an independent trusted split performs final conformalization. The theory shows the final correction removes global threshold shifts, projects the remaining shape error through the boundary density, and gives a three-resource expansion and a benefit-cost rule.
umJRkn3B4L.key_idea: Learn score quantiles with a synthetic-label pinball risk debiased by paired trusted data, then conformalize on an independent trusted split so marginal validity holds.
umJRkn3B4L.evidence: Eight classical regression benchmarks and a human-rating study using labels from general-purpose language models.
umJRkn3B4L.claimed_gains: Substantially improves downstream conditional coverage while preserving marginal validity and producing more compact prediction sets across eight regression benchmarks; no numeric values are stated.

gKpvwexNuO.one_liner: Measures change in Renyi-2 effective dimensionality of attributions across feature aggregation to track grokking and adversarial transfer.
gKpvwexNuO.problem: Existing interpretability methods analyze isolated components or global representations, and it is open whether the structure of attributed contributions admits a general macroscopic observable.
gKpvwexNuO.method: Attribution Vergence quantifies structural reorganization across feature aggregation using Renyi-2 effective dimensionality, under an Aggregation Node formulation covering attention and convolution. It is grounded by attribution preservation, axiomatic compatibility conditions, and an information-theoretic interpretation, with analysis of invariance, bounds, stability, and computation.
gKpvwexNuO.key_idea: Compute the change in Renyi-2 effective dimensionality of attributed contributions across an aggregation node (attention or convolution) as a macroscopic indicator.
gKpvwexNuO.evidence: Experiments on grokking and generative adversarial transfer, with intervention-validated hypotheses about computational mechanisms in grokking.
gKpvwexNuO.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only reports stronger behavioral responses than prior analysis tools.

dQwl13SEMc.one_liner: Timestep-adaptive modulation block that scales text and reference-speech conditions per timestep in flow-matching text-to-speech.
dQwl13SEMc.problem: Flow-matching TTS methods concatenate conditions with the latent state and mix them through shared FC layers, giving identical condition guidance at every timestep although the latent state changes with timestep.
dQwl13SEMc.method: The authors treat text, reference speech, and latent states as conditional distributions over timesteps and derive that guidance depends on the timestep. The TACM block uses the timestep embedding to assign two modulation factors, one for the text condition and one for the reference-speech condition; the abstract is truncated after this.
dQwl13SEMc.key_idea: Use the timestep embedding to produce separate modulation factors for the text and reference-speech conditions, making condition guidance vary with timestep.
dQwl13SEMc.evidence: A derivation of timestep-dependent guidance; the visible abstract does not describe experiments.

27MnPP6eGy.one_liner: End-to-end omnidirectional UAV obstacle avoidance from panoramic image sequences using optical flow and a differentiable spherical motion reasoning module.
27MnPP6eGy.problem: Forward-facing sensors give restricted coverage for omnidirectional avoidance, and existing approaches either have restricted visual coverage or lack designs tailored to panoramic imagery.
27MnPP6eGy.method: Uni-Fly360 uses optical flow as an intermediate representation to reduce the sim-to-real gap. A differentiable spherical motion module uses antipodal consistency and full-sphere constraints to suppress rotation, estimate the ego-translation direction, and build local motion residuals, and is optimized jointly with control.
27MnPP6eGy.key_idea: Exploit antipodal consistency and full-sphere constraints in a differentiable module to suppress rotation in panoramic optical flow and isolate local motion residuals.
27MnPP6eGy.evidence: Experiments on three representative panoramic tasks and transfer to real-world videos.

Y69S27nWgp.one_liner: Feed-forward 4D reconstruction transformer representing motion as shared SE(3) twist trajectories over a few bases with per-pixel assignment weights.
Y69S27nWgp.problem: Existing motion perception methods treat motion as independent point-wise displacements, ignoring that physical objects move under rigid-body SE(3) transformations.
Y69S27nWgp.method: SM4RT introduces Structure-of-Motion, which decomposes scene motion into a compact set of motion bases, each a temporal sequence of 6D se(3) twists, with dense motion recovered through sparse, time-shared per-pixel assignment weights. A parallel motion geometry encoder and decoder jointly infer 3D geometry, world-coordinate motion, and scene kinematics.
Y69S27nWgp.key_idea: Represent scene motion as a compact set of se(3) twist-sequence bases with sparse time-shared per-pixel weights, so points on one object share one rigid trajectory.
Y69S27nWgp.evidence: The abstract is truncated before experiments; no datasets or results are visible.

ug30InmrLu.one_liner: Egocentric loco-manipulation world model spanning humans and robots, trained on 10k hours of human and 3k hours of robot data.
ug30InmrLu.problem: Jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments is hard because of heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision.
ug30InmrLu.method: The authors curate Xp-Data (10k hours of egocentric human data and 3k hours of robot data with unified annotations) and use a unified kinematic representation that encodes locomotion through camera poses and manipulation through projected skeletons, with robot skeletons from embodiment-specific forward kinematics. They also introduce the Xp-Teleop benchmark, and distillation enables real-time rollouts.
ug30InmrLu.key_idea: Encode locomotion as camera poses and manipulation as projected skeletons (robot skeletons from forward kinematics) so one video world model covers humans and several robot embodiments.
ug30InmrLu.evidence: Benchmarks DreamDojo, Psi_0, omega-HOME, and Xp-Teleop from zero-shot to few-shot and full-data post-training, scaling of human pre-training data, and applications in policy evaluation, planning, and world-action modeling.
ug30InmrLu.claimed_gains: Claims the best results on the DreamDojo, Psi_0, omega-HOME, and Xp-Teleop benchmarks and real-time, minute-long rollouts after distillation; no numeric gains are stated.

IAZxLqJCLZ.one_liner: Trains Geometric Readers to emit continuous geometry tokens that a VLM can read, supervised by frozen-VLM-decoded geometry descriptions.
IAZxLqJCLZ.problem: VLMs struggle with metric and multi-view relationships implicit in RGB, and geometry features that are fused or aligned with VLM latents may go unused, since aligned latents can be zeroed without lowering accuracy.
IAZxLqJCLZ.method: First, lightweight Geometric Readers are trained to produce continuous input tokens, supervised by geometry descriptions decoded by a frozen VLM. Then the Readers are frozen while the VLM is fine-tuned on spatial QA with question-conditioned geometry injection; at inference no intermediate geometry chain of thought is generated.
IAZxLqJCLZ.key_idea: Supervise geometry readers through the target VLM's own decoding of geometry descriptions so the tokens match a form it can already read, then freeze them during QA fine-tuning.
IAZxLqJCLZ.evidence: Qwen3-VL-4B with geometry predicted from RGB images, evaluated on MindCube-Tiny and six additional spatial benchmarks with a multi-source QA mixture.
IAZxLqJCLZ.claimed_gains: Reaches 94.3 on MindCube-Tiny and, with a multi-source QA mixture, an average of 70.6 across six additional spatial benchmarks with Qwen3-VL-4B.

gc460WqLcU.one_liner: Turns SVG paths into particles with VLM-inferred physical structure, then animates user drags via a physical diffusion model.
gc460WqLcU.problem: SVG path structure reflects how an image is drawn rather than how the object is physically organized, so unrigged SVGs are hard to animate coherently; existing methods need predefined structure or deform paths directly, and particle models lose path organization.
gc460WqLcU.method: SVG paths are sampled into particles with particle-to-path correspondence, and a VLM infers body groupings, embedded details, and articulated connections into a structured graph. Given a user drag, a pretrained physical diffusion model predicts particle motion with articulated-flow guidance that preserves attachments, and trajectories are transferred back to the original paths.
gc460WqLcU.key_idea: Augment sampled SVG particles with a VLM-inferred graph of groupings and articulations, and guide a physical diffusion model's flow so connected parts keep their attachments.
gc460WqLcU.evidence: The abstract is truncated before experiments; no datasets or results are visible.

jsXr3lFB0R.one_liner: Chooses corrective clicks for SAM-style medical segmentation via Monte Carlo tree search guided by a learned policy-value network.
jsXr3lFB0R.problem: Corrective clicks for promptable segmentation must come from costly experts, and existing automatic prompting uses heuristics or RL policies that do not look ahead and cannot turn extra test-time computation into better masks.
jsXr3lFB0R.method: AlphaClick treats corrective clicking as a sequential decision process and trains a policy-value network with the Dice improvement of each click as reward. At inference, MCTS expands candidate clicks with the policy and evaluates simulated click sequences with the value, without ground truth.
jsXr3lFB0R.key_idea: Run MCTS at test time with a policy that proposes clicks and a value that estimates reachable segmentation quality, so more simulations give better click decisions.
jsXr3lFB0R.evidence: 80 public datasets covering seven imaging modalities.
jsXr3lFB0R.claimed_gains: Dice 0.69 versus 0.43 for the strongest baseline across 80 datasets, with more test-time search giving better masks.

719zzAvpdc.one_liner: Cover-guided one-step diffusion for Live Photo video super-resolution using in-context attention, flow-guided retrieval, and codebook injection.
719zzAvpdc.problem: Existing cover-guided methods mainly enhance individual frames, and complete Live Photo video restoration is hindered by uncertain cover-video correspondence and residual degradation in the cover.
719zzAvpdc.method: LiveVSR jointly models cover and video tokens with bidirectional attention in an in-context framework, with flow-guided local retrieval combining motion cues and content-based matching. Correspondence-guided codebook injection transfers discrete features from a codebook pretrained on high-quality images, and training uses clean and mildly degraded covers.
719zzAvpdc.key_idea: Combine continuous reference features with discrete codebook features of the cover, transferred through contextualized correspondences, inside a one-step diffusion video super-resolution model.
719zzAvpdc.evidence: Comparisons with conventional VSR, reference-guided VSR, and Live Photo image enhancement methods on synthetic benchmarks and real Live Photos.
719zzAvpdc.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only reports favorable visual quality, reconstruction fidelity, and temporal consistency.

08LXl1mANz.one_liner: Resolves scale ambiguity in feed-forward 3D reconstruction by cross-view interaction with a retrieved satellite patch as a metric reference.
08LXl1mANz.problem: Feed-forward reconstruction recovers geometry only up to an unknown global scale, and metric methods need costly large-scale metric annotations or accurate camera calibration.
08LXl1mANz.method: Given coarse position and heading estimates, the method retrieves a local satellite patch and integrates it with a feed-forward reconstruction backbone through bidirectional cross-view interaction. Enforcing consistency between the scene and the satellite reference lets the model infer absolute scale, refine geometry, and estimate metric camera pose.
08LXl1mANz.key_idea: Use a retrieved satellite patch as a global metric reference and enforce scene-satellite consistency through bidirectional cross-view interaction to infer absolute scale.
08LXl1mANz.evidence: KITTI, nuScenes, and Oxford RobotCar for metric depth, multi-view point-cloud reconstruction, and camera localization under cross-dataset and geographic transfer protocols.

QDWOl9ZP6c.one_liner: Selects one sparsity level per layer by minimizing NLL-sensitivity costs under a depth-prefix bound while matching the target mean sparsity.
QDWOl9ZP6c.problem: Existing layer-wise sparsity allocation overlooks pruning-cost variation across sparsity levels, lacks global optimality for discrete allocations, or optimizes Euclidean error rather than the language-modeling NLL.
QDWOl9ZP6c.method: DKNS combines squared weights, input-activation second moments, and squared output-NLL-gradient energies into per-weight deletion costs that aggregate into layer-level state costs. UDPD bounds the cumulative state cost at every depth prefix by the uniform reference allocation, and a three-level lexicographic objective minimizes full-depth cost, then improves prefix cost distribution and sparsity balance.
QDWOl9ZP6c.key_idea: Pick one candidate sparsity per layer by lexicographically minimizing NLL-sensitivity cost, with every depth-prefix cost bounded by the uniform allocation.
QDWOl9ZP6c.evidence: The abstract is truncated before experiments; no models or results are visible.

pI0XNr6iy1.one_liner: Action-conditioned world simulator jointly denoising video and joint-torque with a video diffusion transformer for force-aware rollouts.
pI0XNr6iy1.problem: Existing world models predict only future visual observations, but in contact-rich manipulation distinct physical outcomes can look visually similar, so force signals are needed.
pI0XNr6iy1.method: Built on a pretrained video diffusion transformer, ForceWorld jointly denoises video and force representations to produce multi-view RGB observations and external joint torque. A temporal encoder augments framewise torque embeddings, and torque denoising is modulated directly by action inputs.
pI0XNr6iy1.key_idea: Jointly denoise video and torque in a video diffusion transformer, with temporal torque embeddings and action-modulated torque denoising to capture contact evolution.
pI0XNr6iy1.evidence: Four real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks compared with TACO and two video-prediction baselines, plus closed-loop policy rollouts over minute-scale horizons.
pI0XNr6iy1.claimed_gains: Reduces high-load torque prediction RMSE by 26.6% versus TACO and outperforms both evaluated video-prediction baselines; policy-evaluation success rates correlate with real-world execution at Pearson r=0.956.

qvcRFvYVNK.one_liner: MoE compression that builds a pool by Anchor Coverage, then assigns removed experts via a router-conditioned functional objective.
qvcRFvYVNK.problem: Existing expert compression couples pool construction with the assignment of routed workloads, leaving assignment unoptimized once the pool is fixed.
qvcRFvYVNK.method: ConMoE splits expert compression into constructing a compact pool using Anchor Coverage and assigning the original experts' workloads to it with a router-conditioned functional objective derived from a layer reconstruction bound. It uses unlabeled calibration inputs and keeps the router and expert weights frozen.
qvcRFvYVNK.key_idea: Treat assignment of removed experts as a separate decision, optimized by a layer-reconstruction-bound functional objective rather than parameter proximity.
qvcRFvYVNK.evidence: Three MoE architectures and six zero-shot benchmarks, plus generation workloads for peak GPU memory.
qvcRFvYVNK.claimed_gains: With the pool fixed, functional assignment improves macro accuracy by 1.82 and 0.35 percentage points at 50% and 75% expert retention, and at 50% retention peak GPU memory drops by 29.6-48.4% relative to the uncompressed models.

DzqjXJUOtD.one_liner: Poisons on-policy distillation by editing teacher probabilities to amplify student-generated triggers; Sentinel defends by substituting frozen-student predictions.
DzqjXJUOtD.problem: Prior distillation attacks transfer malicious behavior from a compromised teacher but overlook that poisoned feedback in on-policy distillation can make the student create its own poisoning opportunities.
DzqjXJUOtD.method: Echo Poisoning edits only the teacher probabilities returned during OPD, reinforcing trigger phrases the student starts on its own and teaching attacker-chosen text after each completed trigger. Sentinel replaces suspicious teacher targets with predictions from a frozen copy of the initial student.
DzqjXJUOtD.key_idea: Edit teacher probabilities so the student's own trigger usage grows and each trigger brings poisoned supervision (feedback amplification); defend by swapping suspicious targets for a frozen initial-student's predictions.
DzqjXJUOtD.evidence: Three teacher-student pairs from three model families on math and code tasks, plus evaluation of existing defenses such as divergence masking and an adaptive attack.
DzqjXJUOtD.claimed_gains: Echo Poisoning at least triples the attack success of payload-only poisoning with 1.8 to 8.0 points of accuracy loss; Sentinel keeps attack success at 2.0% under an adaptive attack, while other defenses leave 14.4% to 31.9%.

SU0zAYrmu8.one_liner: Blocks attention flow of visual attention sinks during multimodal pre-training to improve patch-level vision-language alignment in MLLMs.
SU0zAYrmu8.problem: In MLLM pre-training, text-to-image attention collapses onto a few textually irrelevant visual tokens (visual attention sinks) that emerge early and hinder the projector from learning fine-grained cross-modal correspondence.
SU0zAYrmu8.method: ViSAlign temporarily blocks the attention flow of the visual sinks during multimodal pre-training, so the model captures text-relevant visual evidence and learns finer patch-level correspondence.
SU0zAYrmu8.key_idea: Temporarily block the attention flow of visual-sink tokens during pre-training so the projector learns text-relevant patch correspondence.
SU0zAYrmu8.evidence: Analyses of text-to-image attention, sink attention flow, and training dynamics on a pre-trained model, plus experiments across diverse multimodal settings; the abstract is truncated before results.

Ech58pddKU.one_liner: Benchmark and dataset for omni reference-to-video generation, with 12,172 case-specific checklist items for factor-grounded evaluation.
Ech58pddKU.problem: Existing reference-to-video benchmarks cover few reference types and compositions and assess only holistic reference consistency, while training data for omni R2V is costly to build.
Ech58pddKU.method: OmniVBench covers 7 task families and 18 fine-grained tasks across content, motion, style, structure, narrative, and multi-reference settings. Case-specific checklists test whether reference factors are preserved, disentangled and bound to targets, and realized per the instruction; the Omni-R2V Dataset provides training data.
Ech58pddKU.key_idea: Evaluate each case with its own checklist that probes whether intended reference factors are preserved, disentangled, and bound correctly, instead of a holistic consistency score.
Ech58pddKU.evidence: Benchmark and dataset construction; the abstract is truncated before any model results.

TsoU3Bn0ej.one_liner: Multimodal continual instruction tuning with rank-one LoRA Atoms: frozen history reused by benefit, plus adaptive allocation of new Atoms.
TsoU3Bn0ej.problem: Parameter-level or module-level protection insufficiently protects and reuses historical knowledge (causing forgetting, negative transfer, and redundancy) and allocates capacity poorly, ignoring residual demand after reuse and component complementarity.
TsoU3Bn0ej.method: BRACE organizes rank-one LoRA components into Atoms. FixedAtom freezes historical Atoms and task catalogs and selects for reuse by benefit; AdaAtom sets the number and layer-wise distribution of new Atoms from residual demand under a global capacity constraint, and an input diversity loss reduces directional redundancy among new Atoms.
TsoU3Bn0ej.key_idea: Treat rank-one LoRA components as independently managed Atoms: reuse frozen ones chosen by estimated benefit and size new ones by residual demand.
TsoU3Bn0ej.evidence: UCIT and MLLM-DCL with two multimodal backbones, including LLaVA-1.5.
TsoU3Bn0ej.claimed_gains: On LLaVA-1.5, BRACE improves mean final performance over the best prior methods by 6.22 and 4.56; the abstract is truncated, so units and the benchmark mapping are not visible.

tVi4I3wih1.one_liner: Benchmark of 1,200 real-world image-editing queries over 23 tasks, with an open-source pairwise judge PVC-Judge for visual consistency.
tVi4I3wih1.problem: Existing editing benchmarks have narrow task coverage, and standard metrics fail to capture visual consistency, meaning preservation of identity, structure, and semantic coherence.
tVi4I3wih1.method: GEditBench v2 has 1,200 real-world user queries across 23 tasks, including an open-set category. PVC-Judge is a pairwise visual-consistency assessment model trained with two region-decoupled preference data synthesis pipelines and checked on VCReward-Bench, which uses expert-annotated preference pairs.
tVi4I3wih1.key_idea: Train a pairwise visual-consistency judge on region-decoupled synthesized preference data and validate it against expert-annotated preference pairs.
tVi4I3wih1.evidence: Benchmarking of 16 frontier editing models, and PVC-Judge alignment with human judgments on VCReward-Bench.
tVi4I3wih1.claimed_gains: PVC-Judge is best among open-source models and surpasses GPT-5.1 on average; the abstract gives no numeric scores.

KLO0NPf46x.one_liner: Training-free sparse-attention indexer that fuses all heads' linear score term into one dot product per token, skipping the nonlinear correction.
KLO0NPf46x.problem: The indexer in DeepSeek Sparse Attention scores every visible token with multiple query heads, leaving substantial indexing overhead during long-context prefilling.
KLO0NPf46x.method: The weighted-ReLU score is decomposed exactly into a linear term plus a nonlinear correction; with shared keys, the linear terms of all heads fuse into one dot product per token, and LISA selects tokens with this term alone. Two variants add candidate refinement with the original multi-head scorer, one of them sharing candidate pools across layers with layer-specific refinement.
KLO0NPf46x.key_idea: Fuse the linear contributions of all indexer heads into one dot product per token and select tokens by it, dropping the nonlinear correction.
KLO0NPf46x.evidence: RULER on DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.2, LongBench v2 on GLM-5.2, and time to first token on DeepSeek-V3.2 with a 1M-token input.
KLO0NPf46x.claimed_gains: On DeepSeek-V3.2 with a 1M-token input, LISA gives a 4.04x speedup over DSA in time to first token and the four-layer-group variant gives 5.06x, with average RULER scores close to the native baselines.

98KjQO9zI8.one_liner: Lossless certified pruning for sparse-attention indexers: score bounds skip full-head scoring while preserving exact Top-K selection.
98KjQO9zI8.problem: Even with sparse attention, finding the keys to visit requires scoring every key with every indexer head, which is a dense bottleneck inside the attention module.
98KjQO9zI8.method: A seed set gives a lower bound on the selection threshold; nonnegative head projections and joint residual bounds upper-bound positive contributions, and activation-informed aggregation bounds the magnitude subtracted by negative heads, so candidates can be rejected without full scoring. Sparse writeback further reduces memory traffic and selection work.
98KjQO9zI8.key_idea: Reject candidate tokens when an upper bound on their score falls below a seed-set-derived threshold lower bound, so exact Top-K is preserved without full-head scoring.
98KjQO9zI8.evidence: A GPU implementation on English, Chinese, and code workloads against SGLang and LiteTopK, end-to-end tests on GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V3.2, and an analysis of the conditions for exact selection.
98KjQO9zI8.claimed_gains: Accelerates the complete Indexer by up to 2.74x over SGLang and 1.69x over LiteTopK, with end-to-end time-to-first-token speedups of up to 1.94x and 1.50x over the two baselines.

FNUihsoRtu.one_liner: Visual tokenizer for LVLMs that conditions elastic query tokens on pooled spatial anchor tokens to support multiple token budgets.
FNUihsoRtu.problem: Nested spatial pooling causes spectral aliasing that obscures fine detail, while nested query resampling loses grid alignment and degrades spatial grounding under aggressive compression.
FNUihsoRtu.method: PARCEL uses spatial pool tokens as low-frequency layout anchors and conditions elastic query tokens on them through Pool-Conditioned Query Resampling, so queries capture complementary detail and strengthen the pooled pathway even at budgets with no query tokens.
FNUihsoRtu.key_idea: Split feature extraction: pooled tokens act as low-frequency layout anchors, and elastic query tokens, conditioned on those anchors, resample complementary visual details.
FNUihsoRtu.evidence: Evaluations across 30+ benchmarks and two LVLMs against matryoshka baselines at several visual token budgets.
FNUihsoRtu.claimed_gains: Improves the performance-efficiency Pareto frontier and consistently outperforms existing matryoshka baselines across visual token budgets; no numbers are stated in the available abstract.

AVEkJqpXNS.one_liner: Controlled scaling study of pixel-wise Barlow Twins Earth-observation models, yielding a 2B teacher distilled into 44M Matryoshka students.
AVEkJqpXNS.problem: How pixel-wise Earth-observation foundation models scale and how best to spend a fixed pretraining budget are poorly understood.
AVEkJqpXNS.method: Runs 395 training runs within a fixed pixel-wise Barlow Twins family, each evaluated on 15 downstream tasks, and fits a rule that grows encoder and data with budget while projector width stays roughly fixed. It then trains 0.5B, 1B and 2B teachers and distils the largest into compact Matryoshka-embedding students.
AVEkJqpXNS.key_idea: Select and scale pretraining configurations by downstream score instead of pretraining loss, then distill the 2B teacher into compact students with nested Matryoshka embeddings.
AVEkJqpXNS.evidence: 395 controlled runs evaluated on 15 downstream tasks, with the selection advantage checked on 14 tasks not used for selection, and distilled students compared against open and proprietary embedding products.
AVEkJqpXNS.claimed_gains: Pretraining loss barely predicts downstream performance (|Pearson r| < 0.2) and loss-based selection needs roughly 2-5x the compute, the 44-million-parameter student outperforms every open and proprietary embedding product tested, and a 16-dimensional prefix keeps 92% of the 128-dimensional performance at 1/8 of the storage.

qg8QXzZWSw.one_liner: Generation and understanding branches of a unified multimodal model alternate as challenger and solver in RL self-play with evolving data.
qg8QXzZWSw.problem: Recent self-training of unified multimodal models has the generation and understanding branches cooperatively supervise each other rather than challenge each other.
qg8QXzZWSw.method: In each round, the understanding branch proposes candidate descriptions of an image that the generation branch must render back into similar images, and vice versa. Candidates are screened for consistency with their source, the solver trains on the candidate it handles worst, and candidates that defeat one branch seed the next epoch's challenges to the other.
qg8QXzZWSw.key_idea: Each branch's own outputs act as adversarial challenges to the other, the solver trains on its worst-handled consistent candidate, and defeating candidates seed the next epoch.
qg8QXzZWSw.evidence: RL post-training of Janus-Pro-1B evaluated on GenEval, DPG-Bench, and nine understanding benchmarks, plus consistency across repeated samples (truncated in the abstract).
qg8QXzZWSw.claimed_gains: On Janus-Pro-1B, improves GenEval by 2.4 points, DPG-Bench by 1.7 points, and the average over nine understanding benchmarks by 0.7 points.

n70H3twrPz.one_liner: Evicted KV entries are archived as low-rank factors that still participate in attention, scored by a linear expected-attention operator.
n70H3twrPz.problem: Long chain-of-thought generation makes the KV cache the memory and bandwidth bottleneck, and token eviction irreversibly discards history while ranking keys by attention from queries that do not yet exist.
n70H3twrPz.method: LARK combines LEAP, a linear scoring operator equivalent to pre-RoPE expected-query phase scoring that runs as a single projection on cached post-RoPE keys; LACE, a low-rank archival pipeline whose evicted tokens become factors outside the model cache yet still join attention and are re-scored at segment level; and a systems co-design for CUDA-graph-compatible variable-length continuous batching.
n70H3twrPz.key_idea: Compress evicted tokens into low-rank factors that keep contributing to attention, and score keys with a single linear projection equivalent to pre-RoPE expected-query scoring.
n70H3twrPz.evidence: Four models and four benchmarks at a 32k generation limit against eviction-based baselines under shrinking KV budgets.
n70H3twrPz.claimed_gains: At B=2048, near-lossless accuracy with 5.0% of the dense device KV memory and 2.0-3.3x iso-batch throughput.

RpJDA7mgsg.one_liner: Uses dynamic-programming alignment to the policy's shortest success to select which steps get RL updates in VLA training.
RpJDA7mgsg.problem: Final success-or-failure rewards do not show which actions helped, so RL reinforces hesitations in successes and penalizes productive actions in failures, requiring many task attempts.
RpJDA7mgsg.method: DEAL aligns each new episode with the policy's shortest success in the same scene by dynamic programming, matching steps with the policy's own representations, then updates only productive steps in successes and wasted steps in failures. It pairs this with PPO and a recurrent Gaussian action head that gives exact action likelihoods.
RpJDA7mgsg.key_idea: Dynamic-programming alignment of each episode to the policy's shortest same-scene success, using the policy's own representations, identifies productive versus wasted steps without an extra scoring model.
RpJDA7mgsg.evidence: A tabular-model proof under simplifying assumptions, plus experiments on LIBERO (one demonstration per task) and RoboTwin 2.0 compared with SimpleVLA-RL.
RpJDA7mgsg.claimed_gains: DEAL with PPO and the recurrent Gaussian action head yields 97.6% success on LIBERO with one demonstration per task and 80.4% on RoboTwin 2.0, versus SimpleVLA-RL's 96.9% and 66.4%.

FgjKyrV9Us.one_liner: Prunes an LLM to preserve what distillation cannot recover and remove what it can repair, optimizing post-distillation quality.
FgjKyrV9Us.problem: Teacher-student mismatch methods assume a predefined student, while a pruned student could instead be built for post-distillation quality rather than immediate post-pruning quality.
FgjKyrV9Us.method: Distillation-Aware Pruning builds the student by pruning its parent teacher, deciding what to remove by what the intended distillation process can repair.
FgjKyrV9Us.key_idea: Choose which parameters to prune by anticipated repairability under the intended distillation process, rather than by immediate post-pruning quality.
FgjKyrV9Us.evidence: Qwen3-8B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B across multiple tasks and both supervised and on-policy distillation, under matched parameter and training budgets, against independently constructed and conventionally pruned students.
FgjKyrV9Us.claimed_gains: Consistently produces stronger post-distillation students than independently constructed and conventionally pruned alternatives under matched budgets; no numbers stated.

gjmCyG9Yuw.one_liner: Benchmark and outcome-level protocol testing whether video generators reproduce the distribution of physical outcomes across repeated rollouts.
gjmCyG9Yuw.problem: Existing evaluations assess single-video plausibility and do not test whether repeated generations recover the correct distribution of possible behaviors under the same initial observation and action.
gjmCyG9Yuw.method: The paper formalizes probabilistic alignment as a distributional criterion and introduces PAWBench, with PAWEval converting repeated video rollouts into empirical distributions over possible physical behaviors. It also tests whether language prompts or initial noise sampling close the gap.
gjmCyG9Yuw.key_idea: Convert repeated video rollouts into empirical outcome distributions and compare them with reference probabilities of valid physical behaviors.
gjmCyG9Yuw.evidence: Evaluation across 50 scenarios and twelve current video generation systems.

M9QviSmn6P.one_liner: Predicts short-horizon router evolution in MoE reinforcement learning so replayed expert routes stay fresh instead of frozen.
M9QviSmn6P.problem: Routing replay freezes expert routes within each trajectory, which stabilizes MoE RL but ignores how the router evolves under off-policy updates, causing router staleness.
M9QviSmn6P.method: PR2 augments each router with a lightweight evolution predictor that anticipates short-horizon router evolution; during route recording it selects expert sets that anticipate this evolution, and during training it replays them with the current model. The paper bounds recorded-route sensitivity and derives an exact KL threshold for top-k agreement.
M9QviSmn6P.key_idea: Record expert routes from a predicted future router instead of the current one, so replayed routes track router drift between rollout and training.
M9QviSmn6P.evidence: Three MoE models with reuse factors 2, 4 and 8 on math reasoning, plus theory bounding route sensitivity.
M9QviSmn6P.claimed_gains: PR2 achieves the highest average accuracy in all nine comparisons across three MoE models and reuse factors 2, 4 and 8 (the improvement over routing replay is cut off in the abstract).

yhIWxelnhu.one_liner: Benchmark running SRE agents continuously on a live Kubernetes deployment under overlapping seeded faults, scored for correlation, localization, and repair.
yhIWxelnhu.problem: SRE agent benchmarks are episodic with one injected fault, unlike production where incidents overlap, surface through noisy alerts, and often originate from code or configuration changes.
yhIWxelnhu.method: An agent is invoked at a fixed cadence with cumulative alert history and a persistent workspace on a live two-zone Kubernetes deployment while a fault orchestrator injects overlapping faults. Marathon-Score credits each fault for ordered progress through correlation, localization, and repair, computed deterministically from recorded evidence.
yhIWxelnhu.key_idea: Continuous operation with overlapping seeded faults and change-driven repairs deployed through the same build pipeline, scored by ordered per-fault progress from recorded system evidence.
yhIWxelnhu.evidence: Three applications with about sixty faults per run, evaluating 10 methods.
yhIWxelnhu.claimed_gains: Best of 10 methods reaches only 41.3 out of 100; agents often correlate and localize faults but almost never complete repairs while the faults remain active.

7qZq38DaGr.one_liner: SuG aligns 3D CT vision-language models with segmentation-expert priors and lesion-mask-calibrated attention for zero-shot diagnosis and lesion grounding.
7qZq38DaGr.problem: Generalist 3D CT vision-language models lack fine-grained anatomical and lesion awareness, while supervised specialist models do not generalize across diseases and anatomies.
7qZq38DaGr.method: SuG performs specialist-enhanced vision-language alignment using spatial priors from anatomy, class-specific lesion, and class-agnostic lesion segmentors. It also uses lesion masks to calibrate text-conditioned visual attention so disease semantics focus on relevant regions.
7qZq38DaGr.key_idea: Inject segmentation-expert spatial priors (anatomy, class-specific and class-agnostic lesions) into vision-language alignment, and use lesion masks to calibrate text-conditioned visual attention.
7qZq38DaGr.evidence: Evaluated on chest and abdominal CT benchmarks including CT-RATE, Merlin, MedVL-CT69K, and several in-house tumor datasets; the abstract is cut off before the results.

hVrDl0zGtP.one_liner: Vision-only 3D occupancy predictor with projection-aware deformable attention and a coarse-to-fine gated decoder.
hVrDl0zGtP.problem: Reference-point projection alone does not carry camera geometry into later sampling, weighting, and cross-camera aggregation, and high-resolution decoding must balance coarse 3D context with local detail.
hVrDl0zGtP.method: Projection-Aware Deformable Attention (PA-DA) projects learned 3D offsets into each view, applies a Jacobian-based attention bias, and predicts channel-wise fusion weights conditioned on semantic features, projection geometry, and temporal context. A sequential coarse-to-fine decoder concentrates cross-view attention at coarse resolutions and propagates coarse 3D context through gated fusion to guide high-resolution refinement.
hVrDl0zGtP.key_idea: Carry projection geometry through sampling offsets, a Jacobian attention bias, and fusion weights in deformable attention, then pass coarse 3D context to fine scales by gated fusion.
hVrDl0zGtP.evidence: Three benchmarks: SurroundOcc-nuScenes, Occ3D-nuScenes, and SSCBench-KITTI-360, compared with prior methods.
hVrDl0zGtP.claimed_gains: 37.24% IoU / 25.36% mIoU on SurroundOcc-nuScenes, 44.47% mIoU on Occ3D-nuScenes, and 45.06% IoU / 18.13% mIoU on SSCBench-KITTI-360, outperforming compared methods in semantic mIoU on all three.

JpGmIA9Uvn.one_liner: Reconstructs sparse 3D vessels from two binary projections by separately predicting per-ray amount and along-ray allocation, then fusing.
JpGmIA9Uvn.problem: Reconstructing sparse 3D structures from two calibrated binary projections is severely ill-posed because masks show ray-structure intersections but not how much structure a ray contains or its depth distribution.
JpGmIA9Uvn.method: BiAAR splits each ray into amount (how much structure) and normalized allocation (where along the ray), whose product recovers occupancy. From paired masks, signed distance fields, and cameras it predicts view-normalized amounts and a coarse 3D occupancy prior supervised by the full target volume, then combines both with projection evidence by learned fusion and refinement rather than explicit multiplication.
JpGmIA9Uvn.key_idea: Factor each ray's occupancy into explicitly supervised amount and normalized allocation, using a coarse 3D occupancy prior as allocation guidance before learned fusion.
JpGmIA9Uvn.evidence: Simulated ImageCAS and AVDNet-derived ASOCA projections, with ablations on each intermediate prediction and fixed-capacity controls.
JpGmIA9Uvn.claimed_gains: Highest mean Dice and clDice among evaluated methods on simulated ImageCAS and AVDNet-derived ASOCA projections; no numeric values are visible in the abstract.

NXlMNYsCFa.one_liner: Log-alignment profiles record layerwise amplification and activation-scale norms in one forward pass to detect distribution shift and predict failure.
NXlMNYsCFa.problem: Neural networks can stay confident when distribution shift changes their internal responses, so output uncertainty captures such shifts poorly.
NXlMNYsCFa.method: Each probe records two norms during an ordinary forward pass to form a compact profile of layerwise amplification and activation scale. Comparing the profile with reference data gives a score for atypical inputs, and individual coordinates show where responses depart across depth.
NXlMNYsCFa.key_idea: Compare per-layer log-alignment profiles (two recorded norms per layer) against reference data to score atypical internal computation and localize departures by depth.
